controls.reason: Consent forms and logging are primarily legal with marketing and DPO involvement; Legal Advisory accountable.

controls.title: Data Processing Which Requires Consent
controls.control: Include consent management controls in all applicable systems.
controls.additionalControl: Train staff on consent obligations; audit periodically.
controls.reason: Consent management controls in systems require legal oversight with marketing and IT implementation.

controls.title: Consent to Cookies and other Tracking Tools
controls.control: Deploy CMP tools; clearly differentiate between cookie types.
controls.additionalControl: Review third-party scripts and trackers regularly.
controls.reason: Cookie consent management platform and tracking tools are IT security/digital channels responsibility; Compliance verifies.

controls.title: Purpose Limitation
controls.control: Purpose must be documented in RoPA and Privacy Notices.
controls.additionalControl: Conduct DPIAs when changing data use purpose.
controls.reason: Purpose limitation documentation in RoPA and privacy notices is a DPO/Compliance responsibility with data owners.

controls.title: Lawful Basis Clarifications
controls.control: Standard contract templates; auto-deletion triggers for failed onboarding.
controls.additionalControl: Legal review of contracts for DP compliance.
controls.reason: Contract templates and legal basis clarifications are legal advisory responsibilities with procurement and HR support.

controls.title: Reliance on Legal Obligation
controls.control: Legal basis must be documented in RoPA; justify with applicable statutes.
controls.additionalControl: Periodic legal gap analysis between NDPA and other laws; NDPA training for legal and compliance staff
controls.reason: Reliance on legal obligation requires legal documentation and gap analysis; Legal Advisory accountable with Compliance and DPO support.

controls.title: Evaluation of Lawful Bases of Data Processing
controls.control: Lawful basis review as part of DPIA and RoPA maintenance.
controls.additionalControl: Periodic reassessment of lawful basis and risk impact.
controls.reason: Lawful basis review and RoPA maintenance are core data protection compliance activities; DPO is the accountable role within the Data Protection unit.

controls.title: Reliance on Vital Interest
controls.control: Policy for when to invoke “vital interest” basis; log justification.
controls.additionalControl: Internal approval before applying this basis.
controls.reason: Policy for invoking vital interest basis and logging justification is a data protection compliance responsibility; security is a contributor.

controls.title: Reliance on Public Interest
controls.control: Justify basis via DPIA; log reasoning and safeguards.
controls.additionalControl: Compliance review before invoking this basis.
controls.reason: Justifying public interest basis via DPIA and compliance review is primarily a data protection compliance function; legal and IT risk are contributors.

controls.title: Reliance on Legitimate Interest
controls.control: Standard LIA template (from Schedule 8); incorporate into data protection risk reviews.
controls.additionalControl: Annual audits of all legitimate interest-based processing.
controls.reason: Standard LIA template and annual audits of legitimate interest processing are data protection compliance activities.

controls.title: Consideration Regarding Information to Data Subjects
controls.control: Privacy notices on all forms, apps, websites; translated or simplified where necessary.
controls.additionalControl: Use layered privacy notices and automated acknowledgment.
controls.reason: Privacy notices are a data protection compliance requirement; legal, operations, and marketing are contributors. Multiple parties compete for accountability, lowering confidence.

controls.title: Data Privacy Impact Assessment
controls.control: Conduct DPIA using certified DPO; follow Schedule 4; obtain NDPC acknowledgment.
controls.additionalControl: Use automated DPIA checklists during project launch reviews.
controls.reason: Conducting DPIA using certified DPO and following Schedule 4 is explicitly a data protection officer responsibility.

controls.title: Data Privacy Impact Assessment
controls.control: Establish a DPIA policy and procedure; integrate DPIA into project and technology onboarding processes; escalate any privacy risk to Management for review.
controls.additionalControl: Periodic audits of DPIA compliance; Legal review of projects with constitutional/privacy implications
controls.responsibilityText: Data Protection Officer (DPO), ICT Security, Compliance Unit
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: DPO; Head, Project Management; Head, IT Governance
controls.reason: DPIA policy and procedure establishment is led by the DPO; ICT security and compliance are contributors.

controls.title: Data Privacy Impact Assessment
controls.control: Maintain a DPIA checklist; integrate DPIA trigger points into project lifecycle; submit DPIAs to NDPC when criteria are met.
controls.additionalControl: Periodic training of project owners on DPIA triggers; Include DPIA tracking in audit/compliance reviews
controls.responsibilityText: DPO, Legal, IT Governance, Risk Management
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: DPO; Head, Risk & Compliance; Head, Project Management; CIO
controls.reason: Maintaining DPIA checklist and integrating trigger points is a DPO responsibility; legal, IT governance, and risk are contributors.

controls.title: Data Privacy Impact Assessment
controls.control: Maintain an up-to-date register of certified LPDOs; Vet all DPIA engagements for accreditation status.
controls.additionalControl: Periodic vendor verification/audit
controls.reason: Register of certified LPDOs and vetting DPIA engagements is a data protection function; procurement and legal are contributors.

controls.title: Data Privacy Impact Assessment
controls.control: Use DPIA templates that incorporate NDPA & GAID standards; Train staff on GAID.
controls.additionalControl: Internal review before submission
controls.reason: DPIA templates incorporating NDPA & GAID standards and staff training are DPO responsibilities; legal is a contributor.

controls.title: Data Privacy Impact Assessment
controls.control: Compliance calendar; internal NDPA/GAID checklist; early DPO review during IT rollouts
controls.additionalControl: Automate DPIA triggers for sensitive systems; maintain register of all legacy and planned data processing
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: DPO, Head of IT, Compliance Officer
controls.reason: Compliance calendar and DPIA triggers are led by DPO; IT and legal/compliance are contributors.

controls.title: Data Privacy Impact Assessment
controls.control: Use DPIA templates with privacy-by-design elements; review by compliance/legal before filing
controls.additionalControl: Train product/IT teams on privacy-by-design; Embed principles into system development lifecycle (SDLC)
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: DPO, Head of IT Security, Product Development
controls.reason: DPIA templates with privacy-by-design and compliance/legal review are DPO-led; risk, IT security, and product development are contributors.

controls.title: Data Privacy Impact Assessment
controls.control: DPO accreditation checks; internal DPIA template referencing Schedule 4
controls.additionalControl: Periodic training on GAID Schedule 4; use automated DPIA format validator
controls.reason: DPO is explicitly named as primary responsible for DPIA accreditation and template; Compliance is contributor. Internal Audit is the independent verifier.

controls.title: Monitoring, Evaluation and Maintenance of Data Security System
controls.control: Existing IT audit plans, patch management protocols, training schedules
controls.additionalControl: Quarterly cybersecurity reviews; external audit of InfoSec plan; automated monitoring tools
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), IT Risk Team
controls.reason: CISO and IT Security are primary for monitoring and maintaining data security system; Compliance is contributor. Internal Audit verifies.

controls.title: Internal Sensitisation and Training
controls.control: Annual training programs, basic privacy policies, ad hoc sensitisation
controls.additionalControl: Regular compliance audits, internal awareness surveys, periodic refresher courses, automated learning tracking
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Data Protection Officer (DPO), HR Manager, Compliance Manager
controls.reason: HR is listed first and training is an HR function; DPO and Compliance are contributors. Compliance verifies training effectiveness.

controls.title: Deployment of a Data Processing Software by a Data Controller or Data Processor
controls.control: - Pre-deployment DPIA checklist- Internal software review process- Use of standard privacy policy templates
controls.additionalControl: - Privacy design audits- Mandatory legal/privacy review before deployment- Quarterly software compliance checks
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: DPO, IT Dept, App Developers, Legal & Compliance
controls.reason: DPO is primary for DPIA and privacy compliance; IT Security and Legal are contributors. Internal Audit verifies deployment controls.

controls.title: Measures Against Privacy Breach Abatement
controls.control: Incident handling protocol; platform monitoring.
controls.additionalControl: Real-time alert system and NDPC response SOP.
controls.reason: IT Security and DPO share responsibility; IT Security is more accountable for technical breach abatement. Compliance verifies.

controls.title: Data Breach Notification
controls.control: - Incident response plan- Breach detection system- Pre-approved breach notification templates
controls.additionalControl: - Regular training on breach response- Breach response simulation drills- Escalation matrix for breach alerts
controls.reason: DPO is primary for breach notification; IT Security and Legal are contributors. Internal Audit verifies notification process.

controls.title: Data Processing Agreement
controls.control: Contract templates; Legal review; Processor onboarding policy
controls.additionalControl: Annual DPA reviews; Central processor registry with training/registration tracking; Legal/Compliance approval checklist
controls.reason: Legal is primary for contract review and DPA; Compliance and Procurement are contributors. Compliance verifies DPA compliance.

controls.title: Benchmarking with Interoperable Data Privacy Measures
controls.control: Existing privacy frameworks; awareness of international best practices
controls.additionalControl: IDPM review log maintained by DPO; Regular engagement with Commission on evolving IDPMs; Legal approval of IDPM-related applications
controls.reason: DPO is primary for benchmarking and IDPM review; Compliance, IT Security, and Legal are contributors. Internal Audit verifies.

controls.title: Exercise of Right to Rectification
controls.control: Customer data portals with rectification forms; integration with NIMC for NIN verification.
controls.additionalControl: Implement backend audit logs and automated verification prompts before data is submitted permanently.
controls.reason: DPO is explicitly responsible for rectification requests; IT supports backend. Internal Audit verifies.

controls.title: Exercise of Right to Data Portability
controls.control: Portability SOP, data extract tool.
controls.additionalControl: Periodic check of formats and response time.
controls.reason: IT, Legal, and Customer Ops share responsibility; IT is most accountable for data portability tools. Compliance verifies.

controls.title: Exercise of Right to be Forgotten
controls.control: Data subject request workflow; consent management system; defined retention policies.
controls.additionalControl: Automate checks for legal bases before processing erasure; provide clear refusal notices with legal justification when erasure is denied.
controls.reason: DPO is primary for right to be forgotten; Legal and IT are contributors. Internal Audit verifies.

controls.title: Exercise of Right to Lodge a Complaint with the Commission
controls.control: Complaints SOP; escalation tracker.
controls.additionalControl: Designated NDPC Liaison Officer.
controls.reason: Compliance and Legal share responsibility; Compliance is primary for complaint handling. Internal Audit verifies.

controls.title: Data Subject's Standard Notice to Address Grievance
controls.control: SNAG response SOP; grievance log; designated platform access.
controls.additionalControl: Internal grievance officer or team with SLAs.
controls.reason: DPO is explicitly named as primary responsible party for grievance handling; Legal is a contributor. Data Protection unit under Compliance is the natural home for DPO.

controls.title: Parameters for Assessing Emerging Tech
controls.control: Emerging tech assessment checklist; risk review board.
controls.additionalControl: AI Governance Policy; Legal & Ethics Committee review.
controls.reason: Multiple parties (IT, Risk, Compliance) share primary responsibility; risk review board suggests Risk Management ownership. CISO/CIO mentioned as additional but not in role list. Ambiguous due to shared accountability.

controls.title: Capacity Building and CPD Requirements
controls.control: Annual training calendar; training records; CPD policy.
controls.additionalControl: Certification tracking; refresher courses for high-risk roles.
controls.reason: HR is listed first and training calendar/CPD is core HR function. Compliance and DPO are contributors. Verifier is Compliance as it oversees regulatory training compliance.

controls.title: Evidence of Compliance with the NDP Act
controls.control: Maintain compliance documentation; retain audit trails; track all filings with NDPC.
controls.additionalControl: Annual compliance file review and audit trail repository.
controls.reason: DPO is explicitly named as primary responsible for compliance documentation and audit trails. Compliance Officer is contributor. Data Protection unit is appropriate.

controls.title: Supplementary Regulations, Directives and Schedules
controls.control: Regulatory monitoring calendar; subscription to NDPC alerts; policy update triggers.
controls.additionalControl: Assign officer to regulatory watchlist and legal horizon scanning.
controls.reason: Regulatory monitoring and horizon scanning is core Regulatory Compliance function. Legal is contributor. Head of Compliance is accountable role. Confidence moderate due to shared Legal/Compliance responsibility.

controls.act: SEC Guidance on Sections 60–63 ISA 2007
controls.title: Certification in annual or periodic reports
controls.control:
- Establish a robust financial reporting and disclosure policy.
- Maintain internal control framework (e.g., COSO) and conduct quarterly evaluations.
- Set certification protocols for CEO/CFO before report submission.
- Perform internal and external control testing.
- Document and track material weaknesses and remediation actions.
- Implement whistleblower and fraud-reporting channels.
controls.additionalControl:
- Conduct pre-filing assurance reviews with external auditors.
- Use compliance software to flag any missing certifications or data gaps.
- Provide annual training for signatory officers on reporting and internal control responsibilities.
- Include CEO/CFO certification as an item in board compliance dashboards.
controls.responsibilityText: - CEO and CFO - Head of Finance - Audit Committee - Internal Audit and Compliance
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Chief Financial Officer (CFO) - Chief Executive Officer (CEO) - Internal Audit - Audit Committee
controls.reason: CFO is primary signatory for certification; Financial Control unit owns financial reporting policy. CEO co-signs but CFO is more accountable for financial reporting controls. Internal Audit and Compliance are contributors/verifiers.

controls.title: Duty of directors on internal controls
controls.control:
- Implement COSO-based internal control framework for financial reporting.
- Conduct annual internal control risk assessment and testing.
- Require quarterly management sign-offs on control effectiveness.
- Maintain detailed transaction-level documentation and authorization protocols.
- Establish an internal control policy, approved by the board.
controls.additionalControl:
- Appoint a Chief Internal Control Officer or equivalent.
- Require external assurance or reviews on control effectiveness.
- Incorporate control review metrics in board risk dashboards.
- Conduct annual board training on financial control oversight responsibilities.
controls.responsibilityText: - Board of Directors - CEO and CFO - Internal Audit - Compliance and Risk Management - Audit Committee
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Board Risk and Audit Committees - Chief Financial Officer (CFO) - Head of Internal Control/Internal Audit - Company Secretary for Board compliance alignment
controls.reason: Board has ultimate duty but CFO is accountable for implementing internal controls over financial reporting. Financial Control unit is appropriate. Multiple contributors listed.

controls.title: Management's Annual Assessment of, and Report on, the Company's Internal Control over Financial Reporting
controls.control:
- Develop and implement a formal ICFR Assessment Framework.
- Maintain updated ICFR documentation across departments.
- Perform quarterly walkthroughs and controls testing.
- Ensure management certifies controls annually and documents any identified weaknesses.
- Engage independent reviewers to validate assessment findings before annual filing.
- Coordinate with external auditors to align on required control disclosures.
controls.additionalControl: - Use automated tools for ICFR monitoring and testing.- Include ICFR effectiveness metrics in management performance scorecards.- Conduct management and board training on financial control reporting requirements.- Integrate ICFR reviews with annual Internal Audit plan and ERM framework.- Create a control deficiency log with clear ownership and resolution tracking.
controls.responsibilityText: - CEO and CFO- Internal Audit Department- Head of Risk/Compliance- Audit Committee- Board of Directors
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Chief Financial Officer (CFO)- Head of Internal Control / Internal Audit- Compliance Manager- Company Secretary- Audit Committee
controls.reason: CFO is primary for ICFR assessment and certification. Financial Control unit owns the framework. CEO co-certifies but CFO is more directly accountable. Internal Audit provides independent assurance.

controls.title: Duty of auditor to report on internal controls of public companies
controls.control:
- Engage qualified and independent external auditors with clear terms of reference.
- Ensure management shares ICFR assessment and documentation with external auditors.
- Include internal control effectiveness disclosures in the annual report.
- Implement an Internal Audit Review Plan to support management assertions.
- Hold regular audit committee briefings with external auditors to address findings on internal controls.
controls.additionalControl:
- Require pre-issuance internal reviews of the auditor’s control assessment reports.
- Include control assurance KPIs in CFO and Internal Audit performance metrics.
- Develop a management action plan tracker for any auditor-raised control gaps.
- Conduct external quality reviews of audit processes periodically.
controls.responsibilityText: - External Auditor - Chief Financial Officer (CFO) - Internal Control/Compliance Team - Audit Committee - Board of Directors
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Chief Financial Officer (CFO) - Head of Compliance & Controls - Internal Audit - External Auditor - Audit Committee of the Board
controls.reason: CFO is accountable for management's assessment and coordination with external auditors. External Auditor is not internal department. Financial Control unit is appropriate. Internal Audit verifies.

controls.title: Auditor Independence Issues
controls.control:
- Maintain a restricted list of prohibited non-audit services.
- Ensure Audit Committee pre-approves all auditor engagements.
- Conduct periodic reviews of all services rendered by external auditors.
- Establish a policy on auditor independence, including disclosure of all fees paid to the audit firm.
- Include annual auditor independence confirmation in board and regulatory filings.
controls.additionalControl:
- Perform annual third-party review of auditor independence compliance.
- Conduct training sessions for finance, procurement, and audit teams on independence rules.
- Implement an automated conflict-of-interest check before hiring any external service provider related to finance/audit.
- Maintain an external audit service log reviewed quarterly by the audit committee.
controls.responsibilityText: - Chief Financial Officer (CFO) - Head of Compliance - Audit Committee - External Auditor
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Audit Committee Secretary - CFO - Head, Compliance & Controls - Internal Audit
controls.reason: CFO is listed first and owns auditor independence policy from finance side. Audit Committee pre-approves but CFO is accountable for compliance. Multiple parties create ambiguity.

controls.title: Material Weaknesses in Internal Control over Financial Reporting
controls.control:
- Conduct quarterly internal control assessments.
- Maintain a Material Weakness Identification and Escalation Procedure.
- Ensure internal audit reviews include control testing.
- Implement a corrective action tracking system for weaknesses.
- Require management sign-off on all control assessments and disclosures.
- Maintain evidence trail for all evaluations and responses to control failures.
controls.additionalControl:
- Establish a remediation committee to oversee fixes of identified weaknesses.
- Use external consultants for independent review of control environment.
- Integrate material weakness disclosures into board-level risk dashboards.
- Conduct root cause analysis on all significant deficiencies escalated to material weaknesses.
controls.responsibilityText: - Chief Financial Officer (CFO) - Internal Audit - Head of Compliance - Board Audit Committee
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Head of Internal Controls - CFO - Risk & Compliance Manager - Audit Committee Chair
controls.reason: CFO is primary for material weakness identification and remediation. Financial Control unit owns the process. Internal Audit and Compliance are contributors/verifiers.

controls.title: Method of Evaluating
controls.control:
- Inadequate evaluation may lead to undetected control failures, material misstatements, or fraud.
- Absence of evidential matter can result in qualified audit opinions or regulatory sanctions.
- Over-reliance on inquiry or undocumented assessments could cause audit failure and loss of credibility.
controls.additionalControl:
- Conduct control effectiveness testing at least semi-annually.
- Establish a documentation standard for ICFR evidence.
- Train staff on control design and evaluation procedures.
- Use internal control software tools to automate tracking and testing.
- Periodically benchmark control testing practices against industry standards.
controls.responsibilityText: - Internal Audit - Head of Internal Control - CFO - Financial Reporting Unit - Audit Committee
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Internal Control Unit - Internal Audit Department - CFO - External Auditors (for review and attestation) - Risk & Audit Committee
controls.reason: CFO is accountable for evaluation methodology and documentation. Financial Control unit is appropriate. Internal Audit provides independent verification. Multiple contributors listed.

controls.title: Location of the report in annual financial statements
controls.control:
- Establish a checklist for financial statement disclosures, including placement of internal control reports.
- Ensure review of report location during the financial statement sign-off process.
- Include the location requirement in the bank’s internal financial reporting policy.
- Implement a pre-submission review by legal and compliance teams to confirm alignment with regulatory expectations.
controls.additionalControl:
- Periodic compliance training for reporting staff and preparers of the annual report.
- Include report positioning as part of the external auditor’s pre-issuance checklist.
- Maintain a template or style guide for the structure of annual financial statements.
controls.responsibilityText: - Company Secretary - Financial Reporting Unit - Chief Financial Officer (CFO) - External Auditors
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Chief Financial Officer (CFO) - Financial Reporting Unit - Company Secretary - External Auditor
controls.reason: CFO is listed first and is accountable for financial statement sign-off and disclosure placement; Company Secretary and External Auditors are contributors. Compliance verifies alignment with regulatory expectations.

controls.title: Registration of Auditors of public companies
controls.control:
- Maintain a due diligence checklist before auditor appointment or renewal.
- Request and verify SEC registration status of external auditors annually.
- Include registration verification clause in audit engagement letters.
- Maintain a register of approved external service providers.
controls.additionalControl:
- Conduct periodic independent verification of auditor registration status through the SEC.
- Ensure legal and compliance unit reviews auditor engagement documentation.
- Require external auditors to provide annual declarations of compliance with regulatory requirements.
controls.responsibilityText: - Chief Financial Officer (CFO) - Head of Finance - Company Secretary - Board Audit Committee
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Company Secretary - Finance and Accounts Department - Board Audit Committee
controls.reason: CFO leads auditor registration due diligence and engagement; Head of Finance, Company Secretary, and Board Audit Committee contribute. Compliance reviews engagement documentation.

controls.act: Financial Reporting Council of Nigeria Act( Amendment) 2023
controls.title: Power of the Council
controls.control:
- Develop a robust internal control assessment framework.
- Require independent attestation of control systems.
- Enforce a Code of Ethics signed by financial officers annually.
- Mandate CEO/CFO certification of quarterly and annual financial statements.
- Implement real-time monitoring and alert systems for financial/operational changes.
- Integrate disclosure protocols into enterprise risk management (ERM) systems.
controls.additionalControl:
- Conduct annual ethics training for finance staff.
- Include IS control reviews in the internal audit plan.
- Conduct dry runs and simulations of material change disclosures.
- Maintain a compliance dashboard for real-time regulatory tracking.
- Set up a whistleblower mechanism linked to control breaches and ethics violations.
controls.responsibilityText: - Chief Financial Officer (CFO) - Chief Risk Officer (CRO) - Chief Internal Auditor - Chief Information Officer (CIO) - Board Audit Committee
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - CFO (certification, ethics implementation) - CRO (risk control oversight) - Internal Audit (control assessment and attestation) - CIO (IS controls) - Company Secretary/Legal (real-time disclosure compliance)
controls.reason: CFO is accountable for CEO/CFO certification and ethics implementation; CRO, Internal Audit, CIO, and Company Secretary contribute. Internal Audit provides independent control assessment and attestation.

controls.title: Functions of the Council
controls.control:
- Maintain a calendar of statutory filings and ensure alerts/reminders.
- Include submission to FRCN as part of financial reporting checklist.
- Assign clear responsibility to ensure timely board approval and dispatch to FRCN.
- Conduct periodic compliance audits to ensure rules of the FRCN are adhered to by finance professionals and the entity.
controls.additionalControl:
- Include FRCN compliance status in board compliance dashboards.
- Provide training to finance and audit staff on FRCN rules.
- Conduct annual compliance review against all FRC requirements.
- Establish a filing confirmation and documentation system to track all regulatory communications.
controls.responsibilityText: - Company Secretary (regulatory filings) - Chief Financial Officer (preparation and coordination) - Board Secretary - Compliance Officer
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - CFO (for financial statements and coordination) - Company Secretary (for submission and tracking) - Compliance Manager (for enforcing internal compliance mechanisms) - Board Audit Committee (oversight)
controls.reason: Company Secretary is accountable for statutory filings and tracking; CFO prepares and coordinates, Compliance Officer enforces internal compliance. Compliance verifies adherence to FRCN rules.

controls.title: Establishment of Fund of the Council.
controls.control:
- Track and document the bank’s market capitalization at a fixed date annually (e.g., last trading day of the year).
- Maintain a compliance calendar to ensure annual levy is paid before due date.
- Assign compliance responsibility to a named officer (e.g., Financial Reporting Manager).
- Reconcile payment computation against FRCN published framework to ensure correct amount is paid.
controls.additionalControl:
- Conduct annual review of FRCN obligations by external auditor.
- Include this obligation in the bank’s compliance reporting dashboard to management.
- Set up automated alerts/reminders in financial compliance systems.
- Prepare and retain evidence of market cap computation, payment proof, and correspondence with FRCN.
controls.responsibilityText: - Chief Financial Officer (CFO) - Head of Finance and Treasury - Company Secretary (statutory compliance) - Internal Audit (compliance verification)
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - CFO - Financial Reporting Manager - Company Secretary - Compliance Department - Board Audit Committee (oversight)
controls.reason: CFO is accountable for levy payment and market cap computation; Head of Treasury, Company Secretary, and Internal Audit contribute. Internal Audit verifies compliance.

controls.title: Registration of Professionals
controls.control:
- Establish a mandatory pre-appointment check for FRCN registration for all professionals in key roles.
- Maintain a register of professionals within the bank showing their FRCN registration status.
- Include FRCN registration verification as part of due diligence during recruitment and vendor onboarding.
controls.additionalControl:
- Include FRCN registration validation in internal audit reviews.
- Regularly update and cross-check staff and consultants’ FRCN registration status against FRCN’s official portal.
- Include the requirement in vendor engagement policies and terms of reference for consultants or auditors.
controls.responsibilityText: - Chief Compliance Officer - Human Resources Manager - Chief Risk Officer - Head of Internal Audit - Company Secretary
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Compliance Manager - HR & Talent Acquisition - Procurement Unit (for external consultants) - Internal Control & Audit Departments
controls.reason: Chief Compliance Officer leads FRCN registration checks; HR, CRO, Internal Audit, Company Secretary, and Procurement contribute. Internal Audit validates registration status.

controls.title: Material Irregularity
controls.control:
- Develop and maintain a material irregularity response procedure within the audit process.
- Ensure timely escalation of audit findings to the Board Audit Committee.
- Require written response and action plans from management once an irregularity is identified.
- Ensure all directors are trained on responsibility to act on auditor reports.
controls.additionalControl:
- Implement a whistleblower policy for independent reporting of material irregularities.
- Conduct annual training for senior management on responding to auditor recommendations.
- Include this compliance check in internal audit reviews and board evaluations.
controls.responsibilityText: - Chief Compliance Officer - Chief Audit Executive - Executive Management - Audit Committee of the Board
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Head of Internal Audit - Company Secretary - Risk and Compliance Department - Audit Committee Secretariat
controls.reason: Chief Audit Executive is accountable for material irregularity response and escalation; Compliance Officer, Executive Management, and Board Audit Committee contribute. Compliance verifies whistleblower and training compliance.

controls.title: Compliance by Public Interest Entities
controls.control:
- Maintain standard-compliant accounting manuals and update them regularly.
- Establish a compliance checklist for all reports prepared.
- Conduct regular gap analyses between current practices and FRC standards.
- Ensure regular engagement with FRC guidelines, updates, and circulars.
controls.additionalControl:
- Regular training of accounting and finance staff on updates to FRC standards.
- Conduct pre-audit reviews for compliance with FRC frameworks.
- Implement audit trails and version control on reporting templates.
- Use external accounting consultants for complex compliance interpretations.
controls.responsibilityText: - Chief Financial Officer (CFO) - Financial Reporting Unit - External Auditors - Internal Audit - Chief Risk Officer (CRO)
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - CFO - Head of Financial Control - Financial Reporting Manager - Audit Committee - Board of Directors
controls.reason: CFO is accountable for FRC compliance in financial reporting; Financial Reporting Unit, External Auditors, Internal Audit, and CRO contribute. Internal Audit verifies compliance with FRC standards.

controls.title: Monitoring of financial statements and reports.
controls.control:
- Maintain a FRC filing calendar aligned with statutory filing obligations.
- Assign clear responsibilities for preparing and submitting reports to the FRC.
- Establish a checklist for ensuring compliance with FRC rules before submission.
- Maintain up-to-date contact lists for responding to FRC information requests promptly.
controls.additionalControl:
- Periodic training for accounting and finance teams on FRC reporting requirements.
- Develop a report validation workflow that includes legal and compliance review.
- Integrate FRC submission and correspondence tracking into governance dashboards for Board/Executive oversight.
controls.responsibilityText: - Chief Financial Officer (CFO) - Company Secretary - Head of Regulatory Reporting - External Auditors - Chief Compliance Officer
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - CFO - Head of Financial Reporting - Company Secretary - FRC Liaison Officer
controls.reason: Head of Regulatory Reporting is accountable for FRC filing calendar and submissions; CFO, Company Secretary, External Auditors, and Compliance Officer contribute. Compliance verifies reporting compliance.

controls.title: Power of investigation by Council.
controls.control:
- Maintain an up-to-date document inventory system for audit/compliance records.
- Develop and implement a FRC Investigation Response Protocol.
- Designate a liaison officer to interface with FRC investigators.
- Implement data governance and retention policies ensuring documents are accessible and retrievable.
controls.additionalControl:
- Conduct mock regulatory inspections or document drills.
- Ensure offsite and cloud backup of key records.
- Maintain a log of all regulatory requests and responses for audit trail.
- Conduct periodic compliance checks on documentation processes.
controls.responsibilityText: - Chief Compliance Officer - Company Secretary - Chief Audit Executive - CFO - Head of Legal and Governance
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Compliance Department - Legal and Governance Unit - Records Management Officer - Executive Management (for oversight)
controls.reason: Chief Compliance Officer leads FRC investigation response and liaison; Company Secretary, Internal Audit, CFO, Legal, and Records Management contribute. Internal Audit verifies documentation and response protocols.

controls.title: Sanctions for non-compliance.
controls.control:
- Maintain financial review and monitoring systems to detect material misstatements.
- Establish a restatement protocol outlining roles, timelines, and disclosure processes.
- Set up an escalation process for regulatory notices.
- Prepare pre-drafted shareholder communication templates for emergencies.
controls.additionalControl:
- Conduct regular internal and external audits to reduce restatement risk.
- Run scenario-based drills on regulatory interventions.
- Automate tracking of regulatory deadlines and service of notices.
- Train Board and Finance team on regulatory response protocols.
controls.responsibilityText: - Chief Financial Officer (CFO) - Company Secretary - Chief Compliance Officer - Head of External Reporting - Board Audit Committee
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - CFO - External Financial Reporting Team - Company Secretariat - Board Audit and Risk Committee
controls.reason: CFO is accountable for restatement protocol and regulatory notice escalation; Company Secretary, Compliance Officer, and Head of Regulatory Reporting contribute. Internal Audit verifies through regular audits.

controls.title: Sanctions of Public Interest Entities
controls.control:
- Maintain a restatement response plan that defines timelines, roles, and escalation paths.
- Set up automated alerts for receipt of regulatory notices.
- Ensure that financial reporting software allows for rapid generation and revision of financial statements.
- Keep communication templates and board approvals processes ready for rapid deployment.
controls.additionalControl:
- Conduct quarterly regulatory compliance reviews of financial reporting obligations.
- Maintain open channels with FRC and other regulators to get early signals on concerns.
- Engage external consultants or auditors to verify complex corrections before resubmission.

controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Compliance Officer (oversight), Head of Operations/Records, IT Manager (for digital records)
controls.reason: Primary responsibility lists Records Management Team, Compliance Department, and IT/Data Storage Team. Additional responsibility names Compliance Officer for oversight, Head of Operations/Records, and IT Manager. Compliance/AML/CFT is the most accountable unit for record preservation under AML laws.

controls.title: Coomunication of Information
controls.control:
- Maintain up-to-date communication protocols with relevant authorities.
- Ensure authorized access to records for rapid compliance.
- Assign a team for regulatory liaison and urgent document handling.
- Maintain log of all requests and responses.
controls.additionalControl:
- Test response readiness via mock regulatory requests.
- Staff training on information disclosure protocols.
- Legal review before release to unauthorized bodies.
controls.responsibilityText: Compliance Officer, Legal Department, Records Management Team
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Compliance Officer (primary), Legal Advisor (oversight), Records Officer (execution)
controls.reason: Primary responsibility lists Compliance Officer, Legal Department, and Records Management Team. Additional responsibility names Compliance Officer as primary, Legal Advisor for oversight, and Records Officer for execution. Compliance/AML/CFT is the most accountable unit for communication of information.

controls.title: Internal procedures, policies and controls
controls.control:
- Appoint trained compliance officers across all operational units.
- Maintain a centralized AML system for data/information.
- Schedule regular and role-specific AML/CFT training.
- Set up and empower internal audit with AML-specific scope.
controls.additionalControl:
- Independent external AML compliance review annually.
- Quarterly reports from internal audit to executive management.
- HR to track training compliance metrics.
controls.responsibilityText: Chief Compliance Officer (CCO), Head of HR (for training), Head of Internal Audit, Branch Managers
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: CCO (primary oversight), Internal Audit Lead, HR Director, IT/Data Governance Lead (for centralisation)
controls.reason: Primary responsibility lists Chief Compliance Officer, Head of HR, Head of Internal Audit, and Branch Managers. Additional responsibility names CCO for primary oversight, Internal Audit Lead, HR Director, and IT/Data Governance Lead. Compliance/AML/CFT is the most accountable unit for internal AML procedures and controls.

controls.title: Mandatory disclosure by financial institutions and designated non-financial businesses and professions
controls.control:
- Automated transaction monitoring system with value thresholds.
- Daily exception reports for high-value transactions.
- Internal escalation and approval workflow for report submission.
controls.additionalControl:
- Periodic reconciliation of reported transactions with system records.
- Independent audit of high-value transaction reporting compliance.
- Continuous staff training on reporting obligations.
controls.responsibilityText: Compliance Officer, Transaction Monitoring Unit, Operations Manager
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Chief Compliance Officer (overall oversight), NFIU Liaison Officer, Head of Operations
controls.reason: Primary responsibility lists Compliance Officer, Transaction Monitoring Unit, and Operations Manager. Additional responsibility names Chief Compliance Officer for overall oversight, NFIU Liaison Officer, and Head of Operations. Compliance/AML/CFT is the most accountable unit for mandatory disclosure.

controls.title: Prohibition of numbered or anonymous accounts, accounts in fictitious names and shell banks
controls.control:
- Perform Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) on all correspondent banking relationships.
- Require written confirmation from foreign respondent banks that they do not deal with shell banks.
- Periodic audits of international correspondent relationships.
controls.additionalControl:
- Maintain a blacklist of identified shell banks.
- Subscribe to updated international watchlists and FATF advisories.
- Include shell bank checks in onboarding and periodic review checklists.
controls.responsibilityText: Chief Compliance Officer, Head of International Banking, Legal & Risk Unit
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Compliance Unit, Correspondent Banking Relationship Team, Legal Department
controls.reason: CCO is named first and is the most accountable for AML/CFT correspondent banking controls; Legal & Risk Unit and relationship teams are contributors. Periodic audits of correspondent relationships point to Internal Audit as verifier.

controls.title: New products, business practices and technologies
controls.control:
- Conduct pre-launch ML/TF risk assessment on all new products/technologies.
- Use risk-based controls, including enhanced due diligence and transaction monitoring for tech-driven products.
- Maintain a risk register for new technology-enabled services.
controls.additionalControl:
- Involve Compliance in product development lifecycle (design to launch).
- Periodic post-launch risk reviews of new products.
- Incorporate AI/ML tools for enhanced anomaly detection.
controls.responsibilityText: Chief Risk Officer, Chief Compliance Officer, Product Development/Innovation Teams
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Compliance Unit, Product Teams, Internal Audit
controls.reason: CCO and CRO jointly named, but ML/TF risk assessment and compliance lifecycle involvement make Compliance/AML-CFT most accountable; Internal Audit provides post-launch assurance.

controls.act: Guidance Note on Politically Exposed Persons (PEP)
controls.title: CUSTOMER IDENTIFICATION AND VERIFICATION PROCEDURES FOR PEPS
controls.control:
- Embed PEP screening in onboarding forms.
- Use PEP identification checklists/questionnaires.
- Automate screening with PEP databases.
- Implement enhanced due diligence (EDD) for confirmed PEPs.
- Periodically re-screen existing customers.
controls.additionalControl:
- Integrate PEP identification into customer risk scoring system.
- Conduct periodic compliance audits.
- Train staff on identifying and handling PEP relationships.
controls.responsibilityText: Compliance Officer, Onboarding/KYC Teams, Relationship Managers
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Compliance Department, Risk Management, Internal Audit
controls.reason: PEP identification and EDD are core AML/CFT compliance responsibilities; Compliance Officer is named first and Internal Audit conducts periodic compliance audits.

controls.title: Customer Due Diligence
controls.control:
- Conduct PEP screening at onboarding and periodically.
- Use automated watchlists and questionnaires.
- Perform EDD for high-risk/foreign PEPs.
- Maintain a PEP Risk Register.
- Monitor transactions linked to PEPs continuously.
- Reassess risks when customer status or circumstances change.
controls.additionalControl:
- Integrate EDD triggers into core banking system.
- Assign senior management approval before onboarding high-risk/foreign PEPs.
- Conduct annual reviews of PEP profiles.
- Implement geo-political risk analytics tools.
controls.responsibilityText: Compliance Officer, KYC Unit, Relationship Managers, Risk Management Team
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Compliance Department, Risk/AML Unit, Internal Audit for oversight
controls.reason: CDD and PEP screening are AML/CFT compliance functions; Compliance Officer is primary, with Risk Management and KYC as contributors and Internal Audit for oversight.

controls.title: SOURCES OF INFORMATION FOR THE DETERMINATION OF PEPS, THEIR FAMILY MEMBERS & CLOSE ASSOCIATES
controls.control:
- Maintain an up-to-date PEP screening tool.
- Conduct scheduled PEP status reviews.
- Perform multi-source checks (internet, media, commercial databases, customer declarations, competent authority info).
- Enable group-wide information sharing mechanisms.
- Integrate PEP detection questions into onboarding forms.
controls.additionalControl:
- Use automated PEP screening software with AI-based alerts.
- Conduct regular training on PEP detection for front-line and compliance staff.
- Audit trail of all PEP status checks and updates.
controls.responsibilityText: Compliance Officer, Customer Onboarding Team, AML Monitoring Unit, Relationship Managers
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: AML Compliance Unit, IT/Database Admin (for tool updates), Internal Audit (oversight)
controls.reason: PEP screening tool and multi-source checks are AML/CFT compliance responsibilities; Compliance Officer leads, IT supports tool updates, and Internal Audit provides oversight.

controls.title: RISK MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
controls.control:
- Implement automated/manual PEP screening systems.
- Use customer questionnaires and onboarding checks.
- Maintain a structured customer risk profiling process.
- Require senior management approval for all PEPs.
- Monitor PEP accounts regularly using risk triggers.
controls.additionalControl:
- Integrate AI or rule-based alert systems for unusual activity.
- Conduct periodic compliance audits focused on PEPs.
- Maintain a PEP Watchlist and update frequently.
- Provide regular staff training on handling high-risk PEPs.
controls.responsibilityText: Compliance Officer, Risk Management Unit, Relationship Managers, IT (screening systems)
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Head of Compliance, Head of Risk, Internal Audit (oversight), Relationship Managers (first line detection)
controls.reason: PEP risk management system is primarily AML/CFT compliance; Head of Compliance is named in additional responsibility and is most accountable, with Risk Management and IT as contributors.

controls.title: RISK MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
controls.control:
- Implement automated/manual PEP screening systems.
- Use customer questionnaires and onboarding checks.
- Maintain a structured customer risk profiling process.
- Require senior management approval for all PEPs.
- Monitor PEP accounts regularly using risk triggers.
controls.additionalControl:
- Integrate AI or rule-based alert systems for unusual activity.
- Conduct periodic compliance audits focused on PEPs.
- Maintain a PEP Watchlist and update frequently.
- Provide regular staff training on handling high-risk PEPs.
controls.responsibilityText: Compliance Officer, Risk Management Unit, Relationship Managers, IT (screening systems)
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Head of Compliance, Head of Risk, Internal Audit (oversight), Relationship Managers (first line detection)
controls.reason: Duplicate of section 6.1-6.4; same PEP risk management system ownership under Compliance/AML-CFT with Head of Compliance accountable.

controls.title: PEPs AS BENEFICIAL OWNERS
controls.control:
- Mandatory verification of all beneficial owners.
- Risk-based screening to flag PEPs among beneficial owners.
- Automated checks against internal and external PEP lists.
- Escalation for EDD if beneficial owner is a PEP.
controls.additionalControl:
- Conduct periodic reviews and reassessment of beneficial owners.
- Use adverse media and commercial PEP databases.
- Staff training on identifying complex ownership structures.
- Legal review for layered ownership schemes.
controls.responsibilityText: Compliance Officer, Customer Onboarding Unit, KYC/CDD Unit
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Head of Compliance, Relationship Manager, Internal Audit (for assurance), Legal Unit (for complex ownership verification)
controls.reason: Beneficial owner PEP verification is AML/CFT compliance; Head of Compliance named in additional responsibility, with Legal for complex ownership and Internal Audit for assurance.

controls.title: DOMESTIC/INTERNATIONAL ORGANISATION PEPS WHEN NOT HIGHER RISK
controls.control:
- Perform risk assessments to determine the correct PEP risk level.
- Apply standard CDD measures for low/medium-risk PEPs.
- Document justification for risk classification.
- Ensure consistent application of procedures across branches.
controls.additionalControl:
- Include the customer in periodic PEP re-screenings.
- Provide guidance for reassessing risk if new information emerges (e.g. adverse media, career changes).
controls.responsibilityText: Compliance Officer, Customer Due Diligence (CDD) Team
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Risk Management Unit, Compliance Department, Relationship Manager
controls.reason: Risk classification and standard CDD for lower-risk PEPs are compliance-owned; Compliance Officer leads, Risk Management contributes, and Compliance provides independent review.

controls.title: PERIODIC REVIEW FOR PEP CUSTOMERS
controls.control:
- Establish a risk-based schedule for reviewing PEP accounts.
- Update PEP risk profiles periodically.
- Flag and investigate deviations in expected account behavior.
- Review PEP database regularly to capture status changes.
controls.additionalControl:
- Implement automated alerts for unusual activity.
- Use PEP re-screening tools to capture updated statuses.
- Escalate high-risk findings to senior management.
controls.responsibilityText: Compliance Officer, Relationship Managers, Risk Management Team
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Compliance Department, Internal Audit, and Business Units managing PEP relationships
controls.reason: Periodic PEP review is AML/CFT compliance; Compliance Officer is primary, Relationship Managers and Risk Management contribute, Internal Audit verifies.

controls.title: Record Keeping
controls.control: - Centralized digital archiving system- Documented Record Retention Policy- Access control logs- Retrieval SLA for regulatory data requests
controls.additionalControl: - Regular audits of record storage systems- Compliance drills (simulated requests)- Data integrity and backup validation routines- Defined escalation matrix for record-related requests
controls.responsibilityText: - Chief Compliance Officer (CCO)- Records & Information Management Unit- IT/Database Administrators
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Chief Compliance Officer (CCO)- Head of Data Management- Internal Audit Unit
controls.reason: Record keeping for AML/CFT is owned by CCO; Records & Information Management and IT/Database Admin are contributors, Internal Audit verifies record storage and compliance drills.

controls.title: Reporting
controls.control:
- Implement real-time transaction monitoring systems for PEP accounts.
- Establish PEP-specific monitoring rules.
- Train staff to escalate suspicious behavior for PEPs.
- Maintain a PEP activity watchlist.
controls.additionalControl:
- Conduct automated adverse media screening.
- Periodically audit STR filings related to PEPs. 
- Escalate alerts involving high-value or unusual cross-border transactions.
controls.responsibilityText: Compliance Officer, Transaction Monitoring Unit, Operations Department
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Compliance Department (STR Filing), Risk Monitoring Unit, Internal Audit
controls.reason: PEP transaction monitoring and STR filing are AML/CFT compliance; Compliance Officer leads, Transaction Monitoring and Operations contribute, Internal Audit audits STR filings.

controls.title: Training and Education
controls.control:
- Develop a structured AML/CFT/CPF training plan.
- Include PEP risk handling modules.
- Use case-based learning.
- Mandate periodic assessments to ensure knowledge retention.
controls.additionalControl:
- Maintain training logs and attendance records.
- Conduct periodic competency tests.
- Engage external experts for advanced PEP training.
controls.responsibilityText: Human Resources (Training), Compliance Officer, Departmental Heads
controls.reason: HR (Training) is listed first and owns delivery of the training plan; Compliance provides content and Internal Audit validates. Head of HR is the accountable role for HR training delivery.

controls.act: Guidelines on Targeted Financial Sanctions Related to Terrorism and Terrorism Financing
controls.title: Obligations on Financial Institutions to Implement TFS
controls.control: Use of sanctions screening tools, regular watchlist checks, automated alerts, staff training
controls.additionalControl: Real-time monitoring, auto-flagging of listed names, instant sanctions list updates
controls.reason: CCO and Compliance Unit are the primary responsible parties for TFS implementation; IT/Monitoring supports. CCO is the accountable role.

controls.title: Alert System
controls.control: Subscription to automated email alerts from UN and NIGSAC platforms; regular compliance checks
controls.additionalControl: Set up a monitoring calendar to verify list updates and email alerts weekly
controls.reason: CCO is listed first as responsible for alert subscription and compliance checks; IT provides support. CCO is accountable.

controls.title: Screening
controls.control: Automated sanction screening tools; real-time transaction screening; trained compliance team; periodic full customer base screening; documented procedures for potential and confirmed matches.
controls.additionalControl: Daily watchlist updates; periodic audits of screening logs; enhanced training on match escalation protocol; integrated alerts with onboarding and transaction platforms.
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Compliance Officer, IT & Risk Management Teams
controls.reason: CCO and AML/CFT Unit are primary for screening; IT and Risk Management are contributors. CCO is accountable.

controls.title: Application of targeted financial sanctions
controls.control: Real-time sanctions screening system; immediate transaction freeze protocols; periodic staff training; access to updated Sanctions Lists; defined escalation procedures.
controls.additionalControl: Automated freeze triggers in transaction processing systems; daily reconciliation of sanctioned accounts; internal audit testing of freeze timelines; escalation matrix for sanction matches.
controls.responsibilityText: Chief Compliance Officer, Sanctions Compliance Unit
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Compliance Officer, Sanctions Monitoring Team, IT Security Department
controls.reason: CCO and Sanctions Compliance Unit own application of TFS; IT Security supports. CCO is accountable.

controls.title: Categories of Funds Subject to Freezing Obligations
controls.control: Comprehensive sanctions screening across all asset classes; internal asset classification register; digital currency monitoring; asset freeze procedures; cross-functional verification with finance, operations, and IT units.
controls.additionalControl: Integration of screening tools with asset registers; periodic review of asset holdings; automated detection and flagging of asset categories linked to sanctioned persons; refresher training for treasury and investment staff on new asset types (e.g., virtual currencies).
controls.responsibilityText: Chief Compliance Officer, Treasury Department, Asset Management Unit
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Compliance Officer, Asset Management Lead, Treasury Operations, IT Systems Monitoring
controls.reason: CCO is listed first and sanctions screening is a compliance function; Treasury and Asset Management are contributors. CCO accountable.

controls.title: Target for Freezing Measures
controls.control: Enhanced due diligence, ownership and control structure analysis, relationship mapping tools, and regular updates to screening software.
controls.additionalControl: Implement automated beneficial ownership tracing; conduct periodic reviews of related-party linkages; obtain declarations on control from customers during onboarding and periodic KYC updates.
controls.responsibilityText: Compliance Officer, Legal Unit, Customer Due Diligence (CDD) Team
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Compliance Department, Relationship Managers, Legal Advisory Team
controls.reason: Compliance Officer and CDD Team lead EDD and ownership analysis; Legal supports. Compliance Officer is accountable.

controls.title: Receipt of additional funds into frozen accounts
controls.control: Open and maintain designated frozen accounts; system flagging of inflows; automatic routing of interest and payments to designated accounts; prompt reporting mechanism.
controls.additionalControl: Automate alerts for inflows into frozen accounts and auto-generate NFIU report templates; periodic reconciliation to ensure no misrouting of funds.
controls.responsibilityText: Compliance Officer, Operations Department, Treasury Unit
controls.reason: Compliance Officer is listed first for frozen account handling; Operations and Treasury execute. Compliance Officer accountable.

controls.title: Approval for usage of frozen funds by designated persons and entities on the UN List
controls.control: Internal protocol to reject all usage requests unless accompanied by NSC written directive; documented implementation of approval; timely reporting to NSC.
controls.additionalControl: Maintain a log of all frozen fund access requests; conduct regular compliance audits on frozen account activity; integrate NSC communication into compliance workflow system.
controls.responsibilityText: Compliance Officer, Legal Department, Account Services
controls.reason: Compliance Officer leads protocol for frozen fund usage requests; Legal and Account Services support. Compliance Officer accountable.

controls.title: Reporting Requirements
controls.control:
- Automated alert systems for name matching. 
- Detailed STR templates capturing historical fund relationships. 
- Block or reject functionality built into transaction systems. 
- Clear workflow for reporting attempted transactions. - Secure reporting line to NFIU with internal escalation protocols.
controls.additionalControl:
- Conduct periodic back-testing to detect missed attempted transactions. 
- Ensure that historical account activity (up to 5 years) is readily retrievable and linked to STR framework. 
- Use AI-based tools to flag high-risk profiles and related parties.
controls.responsibilityText: - Chief Compliance Officer - AML Reporting Officer - Transaction Monitoring Team
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - AML/CFT Desk Officer (Initiation) - Chief Compliance Officer (Approval) - IT/Data Team (Historical account review)
controls.reason: CCO is listed first and approves reporting; AML Reporting Officer and Transaction Monitoring execute. CCO accountable.

controls.title: Additional Obligations for Fis
controls.control:
- Real-time automated screening system for name matching and sanctions alerts.
- Immediate escalation and freezing protocols.
- TFS Compliance Manual outlining procedures for CDD, trade finance compliance, and escalation.
- Staff training on handling TFS alerts and reporting requirements.
controls.additionalControl:
- Regular audit of sanctions screening process.
- Periodic review of sanctions lists integration.
- Mock drills for rapid freezing response.
- Annual review of TFS compliance policy.
controls.responsibilityText: Chief Compliance Officer, Sanctions/AML Compliance Team, IT/Security Teams, Operations
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Compliance Department (reporting & monitoring), IT (screening systems), Internal Audit (review), Operations (execution of freeze/lift)
controls.reason: CCO and Sanctions/AML Compliance Team are primary for TFS obligations; IT and Operations support. CCO accountable.

controls.title: Record Keeping
controls.control: Use centralized digital record-keeping system with tagging for TFS actions; ensure consistent file naming and tracking.
controls.additionalControl: Conduct periodic audits of TFS records; maintain secure backup; assign access controls and logging.
controls.reason: Compliance Officer and Records Management Unit own TFS record keeping; IT supports. Compliance Officer accountable.

controls.act: Terrorism (Prevention and prohibition) Act, 2022
controls.title: Freezing order in respect of designated persons or entities
controls.control:
- Real-time automated name screening against UN/Nigeria Sanctions Lists
- Daily updates of sanctions watchlists
- Policy for immediate account freezing and escalation
- STR reporting system integrated with sanctions alerts
controls.additionalControl:
- Periodic testing and audit of screening systems
- Staff training on identifying designated persons
- Clear SOPs for escalation to management and regulatory bodies
controls.responsibilityText: Chief Compliance Officer, Head of Sanctions Desk, AML/CFT Officer
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Compliance Department, Sanctions Monitoring Team, MLRO
controls.reason: Chief Compliance Officer is the most accountable role for sanctions freezing orders; AML/CFT unit within Compliance owns the control, with sanctions monitoring and MLRO as contributors.

controls.title: Freezing obligation in respect of Proliferation Financing
controls.control:
- Automated name-screening system against the UN and Nigeria Sanctions Lists.
- Immediate alert escalation procedures.
- STR filing checklist and audit trail tracking system.
- Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for asset freezing and notification.
controls.additionalControl:
- Daily sanctions list update and reconciliation.
- Periodic audit of sanctions implementation process.
- Staff refresher training on handling sanctions and STR obligations.
- Compliance testing and scenario simulations.
controls.responsibilityText: Chief Compliance Officer (CCO), Sanctions Compliance Officer, Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO)
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Compliance Department, IT (Screening Systems), Legal and Regulatory Affairs Unit
controls.reason: CCO is accountable for proliferation financing freezing obligations; AML/CFT unit is the natural owner, with IT and Legal as contributors.

controls.title: Freezing order on banks or other financial institutions
controls.control:
- Centralized alert system for freezing orders.
- Standard protocol to escalate to legal and compliance units.
- Restriction flagging in core banking system.
- Internal checklist to track compliance with orders (information supply, documentation, transaction blocks).
controls.additionalControl:
- Regular training for branch managers and operations officers.
- Simulated drills to test account freezing and information supply response.
- Independent audit reviews of account freeze procedures.
controls.responsibilityText: Chief Compliance Officer (CCO), Branch Manager, Legal & Regulatory Unit, MLRO
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Branch Operations Team, Compliance Department, Legal Department
controls.reason: CCO is most accountable for freezing orders on banks; branch and legal units are contributors. Branch Manager is not the single accountable owner.

controls.title: Confiscated and Forfeited Assets Account
controls.control:
- Dedicated procedures for handling and transferring forfeited funds.
- Mandatory use of designated Confiscated and Forfeited Assets Account.
- Dual-authorization system for any transaction involving forfeited assets.
- Escalation and reporting to appropriate asset management authority.
controls.additionalControl:
- Independent review and audit of forfeited funds processes.
- Ongoing staff training on asset forfeiture obligations and designated accounts.
- Integration of proceeds of crime tracking software.
controls.responsibilityText: Compliance Officer, Treasury Operations, Legal Department, MLRO
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Legal & Compliance Units, Treasury Department, AML Unit
controls.reason: Compliance Officer is listed first and accountable for confiscated/forfeited assets account procedures; Treasury and Legal are contributors.

controls.title: Obligation to develop counter-financing of terrorism programmes and strategies
controls.control:
- Establish robust CFT policies and frameworks.
- Conduct ongoing risk assessments to detect unusual patterns.
- Deploy automated transaction monitoring systems to flag suspicious activities.
- Escalate and investigate flagged transactions.
controls.additionalControl:
- Periodic audits and external reviews of the CFT programme.
- Regular employee training on CFT risk indicators.
- Maintain up-to-date terrorist watchlists integrated with transaction monitoring.
controls.responsibilityText: Chief Compliance Officer, MLRO, Risk Management Department
controls.reason: CCO is accountable for CFT programmes; MLRO and Risk Management contribute. AML/CFT unit is the correct unit.

controls.title: Obligation to report suspicious transactions
controls.control:
- Automated transaction monitoring system to flag suspicious activity.
- STR (Suspicious Transaction Report) filing procedures aligned with 24-hour rule.
- Internal escalation protocol for urgent review and reporting.
- PEP and Sanctions list screening integration.
controls.additionalControl:
- Periodic refresher training for all compliance and frontline staff.
- Ongoing audit of STR compliance timelines.
- Regular testing of automated alert systems and manual override functionality.
controls.responsibilityText: Chief Compliance Officer (CCO), MLRO, Compliance Unit
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: MLRO (STR preparation and submission), CCO (oversight and governance), Compliance Analysts (detection and investigation)
controls.reason: CCO has oversight and governance for STR reporting; MLRO prepares and submits, analysts detect. AML/CFT unit owns the control.

controls.act: Guidelines on Targeted Financial Sanctions Relating to Proliferation Financing
controls.title: Alert System
controls.control:
- Ensure active and verified subscription to the UN and NIGSAC alert systems.
- Assign a responsible officer to monitor updates and notify relevant departments.
- Integrate alert systems with sanction screening software.
controls.additionalControl:
- Test alert systems periodically to confirm receipt.
- Maintain evidence/logs of alert emails received and reviewed.
- Automate sanctions list downloads for real-time update in screening tools.
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Compliance Officer (subscription oversight); IT/Systems Team (technical integration); Sanctions Screening Team (monitoring and action)
controls.reason: Compliance Officer is accountable for alert system subscription and oversight; IT provides technical integration. AML/CFT unit is appropriate.

controls.title: Institutional PF Risk Assessment
controls.control:
- Develop and maintain a PF Risk Assessment Framework
- Conduct periodic risk assessments covering geographic, customer, and product/service risks
- Implement enhanced due diligence and sanctions screening for higher-risk areas
- Integrate PF risk considerations into onboarding and transaction monitoring
controls.additionalControl:
- Perform annual PF risk reviews
- Use external PF risk data sources (e.g., FATF, UN)
- Conduct internal audits of PF risk controls
- Train staff specifically on PF risks and TFS implementation
controls.responsibilityText: Chief Compliance Officer / Risk Management Department
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Chief Compliance Officer (policy & framework); Risk Management (risk assessment); Sanctions Screening Team (implementation)
controls.reason: CCO owns PF risk assessment framework; Risk Management contributes. AML/CFT unit is the correct unit for PF risk.

controls.title: Screening
controls.control:
- Deploy automated screening tools with real-time alerts
- Perform daily batch screening and immediate screening upon list updates
- Maintain Sanctions List integration in onboarding and transaction systems
- Define workflows for handling matches (Confirmed, False Positive, Potential Match)
- Maintain audit trail of all screening actions and decisions
controls.additionalControl:
- Conduct regular system validations and list updates
- Provide sanctions screening training
- Run mock drills/simulations
- Review past financial activity of designated and related parties
- Use secondary validation through NSC when in doubt
controls.responsibilityText: Compliance Officer Sanctions & AML Monitoring Unit IT/System Admin for automated screening
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Compliance & Sanctions Team (Operational) Head of Risk (Oversight) IT/Security (Screening System Maintenance)
controls.reason: Compliance Officer is accountable for screening operations; IT and Risk contribute. AML/CFT unit owns sanctions screening.

controls.title: Application of targeted financial sanctions
controls.control:
- Integrate automated systems to identify and freeze assets immediately upon a confirmed match
- Maintain a workflow escalation procedure for handling designated matches
- Restrict access to frozen accounts and ensure blocking of outgoing transactions
- Establish a communication protocol for informing affected parties about appeal mechanisms via NSC
- Maintain audit logs of all freezing actions and related correspondence
controls.additionalControl:
- Conduct regular mock testing of the freezing procedures
- Maintain a watchlist review committee to verify complex cases
- Periodic training for staff on "freezing without delay" principle
- Implement an automated alert escalation system to ensure no delays in freezing actions
controls.responsibilityText: - Compliance Officer (Sanctions) - AML/CFT Desk - Operations Department - IT Security (System-level blocks)
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Head of Compliance (Final authority for action) - Sanctions Monitoring Officer (Execution) - Internal Audit (Periodic review of freezing processes)
controls.reason: Head of Compliance is final authority for TFS application; Operations and IT contribute. AML/CFT unit is correct.

controls.title: Receipt of additional funds into frozen accounts
controls.control:
- Automate flagging and routing of incoming transactions to frozen accounts.
- Maintain a frozen account monitoring register.
- Develop a process flow for Escrow account creation and documentation.
- Implement internal workflow for timely reporting to the NFIU.
controls.additionalControl:
- Regular reconciliation of frozen accounts to monitor for unexpected credits.
- Establish automated triggers for report generation and alerts for credits to frozen accounts.
- Maintain communication templates for prompt notification to the Attorney-General.
controls.responsibilityText: - Compliance Department (Sanctions Unit) - Operations Department - Legal Department (for notification to Attorney-General)
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Head of Compliance (Oversight) - Sanctions Compliance Officer (Execution and NFIU filing) - Legal Officer (Communication with Attorney-General)
controls.reason: Head of Compliance has oversight for frozen account receipts; Sanctions Unit executes, Legal notifies. AML/CFT unit owns the control.

controls.title: Condition for Approval for usage of frozen funds by designated persons and entities under the UN Consolidated List
controls.control:
- Maintain a central register of frozen accounts.
- Require written NSC approval before executing any debit or release.
- Implement a workflow checklist before processing any transaction on a frozen account.
controls.additionalControl:
- Embed approval verification step into core banking system.
- Conduct periodic compliance audits of all frozen fund approvals.
- Maintain a secure archive of all NSC approvals and reports sent.
controls.responsibilityText: - Compliance Officer (Sanctions Desk) - Operations Department (Funds release execution) - Legal Department (Verification and interpretation of NSC approval)
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Head of Compliance (Oversight) - Sanctions Compliance Officer (Execution & Reporting to NSC) - Legal Officer (Validation of NSC directive)
controls.reason: Head of Compliance oversees approval for frozen fund usage; Operations executes, Legal validates NSC approval. AML/CFT unit is correct.

controls.title: Reporting Requirements
controls.control:
- Implement automated systems to detect and flag blocked, rejected, or failed transactions involving designated names.
- Maintain a log of attempted transactions tied to CDD failures or sanctions list matches.
- Escalate all flagged incidents to Compliance for review and STR filing.
controls.additionalControl:
- Conduct real-time transaction screening with sanction list integration.
- Include attempted transaction scenarios in employee training.
- Require dual authorization for rejection of suspicious high-risk transactions.
controls.responsibilityText: - Sanctions Compliance Unit - Operations Department (Transaction flagging) - AML Monitoring Team
