The most accountable function is AML/CFT within Compliance, with the Head of Compliance overseeing STR filing. Operations and IT are contributors. Internal Audit provides independent verification.

controls.title: Additional Obligations for Fis
controls.control:
- Maintain active subscription to NSC/CBN alert systems.
- Daily screening against updated sanctions lists.
- TFS response protocol and escalation procedures documented.
- Enforce no tipping-off protocols.
- Incorporate TFS clauses into Trade Finance and CDD policies.
controls.additionalControl:
- Set up automated alerts/workflows for TFS notifications.
- Conduct quarterly staff drills and refreshers on TFS procedures.
- Ensure segregation of duties to prevent internal leaks or lapses.
- Conduct annual independent TFS compliance audits.
controls.responsibilityText: - Sanctions Compliance Unit - Legal & Regulatory Compliance - Internal Audit - Trade Finance & Operations Units
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Chief Compliance Officer (Oversight) - TFS Desk Officer (Execution) - Training Manager (Staff education & awareness) - Head of Trade & Operations (Trade-related compliance)
controls.reason: Primary responsibility text includes Sanctions Compliance Unit, Legal & Regulatory Compliance, Internal Audit, and Trade Finance & Operations Units. The accountable owner is the Sanctions Compliance function within AML/CFT, with the Chief Compliance Officer providing oversight. Legal, Internal Audit, and Trade Operations are contributors. Internal Audit verifies independently.

controls.title: Record Keeping
controls.control: - Standard Operating Procedures for documentation of all TFS-related actions- Secure digital storage system with indexing and search functionality- Periodic audit of TFS recordkeeping practices
controls.additionalControl: - Automation of record capture and tagging for every TFS event- Staff training on documentation standards- Quarterly review of data accessibility and backup protocols
controls.responsibilityText: Chief Compliance Officer (CCO), Records/Documentation Unit, IT/Data Management Team
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: CCO, Head of Operations, Head of Records Management, IT Support Lead
controls.reason: Primary responsibility text names Chief Compliance Officer, Records/Documentation Unit, and IT/Data Management Team. The CCO is the most accountable role, with records management and IT as contributors. Internal Audit conducts periodic audits of recordkeeping.

controls.act: Exposure of Draft Baseline Standards for Automated Anti-Money Laundering (AML) Solutions
controls.title: User Interface & Customization
controls.control:
- Procurement of AML tools with customization and update features.
- Conduct User Acceptance Testing (UAT) before deployment.
- Establish internal procedures for updating rules/scenarios without vendor reliance.
- Provide training and onboarding guides for staff using the AML system.
- Ensure dashboard functionality for real-time alerting and case tracking.
controls.additionalControl:
- Regular testing and feedback loop from end-users to improve usability.
- Ensure a Service-Level Agreement (SLA) exists with the vendor for timely support.
- Integrate the dashboard with other compliance tools for seamless oversight.
- Simulate language and currency support across all relevant jurisdictions.
controls.responsibilityText: - Chief Compliance Officer - Head of IT/Technology - AML System Administrator
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - AML Technology Implementation Team - Compliance Operations Team - Internal Audit (for system effectiveness reviews)
controls.reason: Primary responsibility text lists Chief Compliance Officer, Head of IT/Technology, and AML System Administrator. The CCO is accountable for AML system procurement and customization, with IT and the system administrator as contributors. Internal Audit reviews system effectiveness.

controls.title: System Integration & Scalability
controls.control:
- Obtain CBN approval before entering shared service arrangements.
- Ensure AML system includes secure APIs or data ports for other system connections.
- Conduct integration testing with all target systems (e.g., core banking, KYC, STR reporting).
- Build data import/export utilities for non-integrated systems.
- Use encryption protocols for secure data transmission.
controls.additionalControl:
- Conduct periodic scalability stress tests on AML tools.
- Maintain documentation and logs for data transfers and system linkages.
- Assign dedicated IT compliance liaisons to ensure smooth integration with future platforms.
- Include integration KPIs and service level commitments in vendor contracts.
controls.responsibilityText: - Chief Technology Officer (CTO) - Chief Compliance Officer (CCO) - Head of IT Infrastructure - AML Implementation Lead
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Technology Integration Team - Compliance System Admin - Internal Audit (for post-implementation review)
controls.reason: Primary responsibility text includes Chief Technology Officer, Chief Compliance Officer, Head of IT Infrastructure, and AML Implementation Lead. System integration and scalability are primarily IT responsibilities, with Compliance providing AML requirements. Internal Audit conducts post-implementation reviews.

controls.title: Sanction List and PEP Training
controls.control:
- Deploy an AML tool that integrates with UN, OFAC, EU, and Nigerian sanctions lists.
- Implement AI-fuzzy matching engines for effective name-matching.
- Set up automated pipelines to ensure real-time sanctions list updates.
- Maintain and regularly update internal watchlists.
- Integrate and periodically update PEP databases from credible global sources.
- Activate adverse media scanning tools and link to internal case management systems.
controls.additionalControl:
- Conduct regular tuning and validation of fuzzy match algorithms to minimize false positives/negatives.
- Carry out internal audits of sanction list updates and screening processes.
- Train staff on interpreting AI-flagged results and adverse media alerts.
- Monitor vendor reliability for sanctions list feed and data quality.
controls.responsibilityText: - Chief Compliance Officer (CCO) - AML Operations Manager - Head of Technology - Head of Risk & Controls
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Compliance Technology Team - AML Screening Team - Internal Audit (for independent review)
controls.reason: Primary responsibility text lists Chief Compliance Officer, AML Operations Manager, Head of Technology, and Head of Risk & Controls. The CCO is accountable for sanctions and PEP screening, with IT and Risk as contributors. Internal Audit independently reviews screening processes.

controls.title: Transaction Monitoring & Risk-Based Analysis
controls.control:
- Conduct regular stress testing and scenario analysis on AML transaction monitoring systems.
- Define a measurable benchmark (e.g., ≤10% false positives) as a threshold for system performance.
- Implement system tuning protocols to optimize detection rules and minimize false positives.
- Use AI/ML analytics to improve risk detection precision.
controls.additionalControl:
- Maintain a dashboard to track false positive metrics and performance trends.
- Engage external validators or third-party auditors for independent performance testing.
- Conduct root cause analysis on spikes in false positives and retrain detection models.
controls.responsibilityText: - Head of Compliance - AML Systems Analyst - Internal Audit - Head of IT Risk Management
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Compliance Risk Team - AML Monitoring Unit - Data Science/Analytics Team - External System Validator (where used)
controls.reason: Primary responsibility text includes Head of Compliance, AML Systems Analyst, Internal Audit, and Head of IT Risk Management. Transaction monitoring and tuning are primarily Compliance responsibilities, with Risk and IT as contributors. Internal Audit provides independent validation.

controls.title: Customer Due Diligence (CDD), Know Your Customer (KYC) & Know Your Customer’s Business (KYB)
controls.control:
- Deploy automated onboarding tools that perform real-time KYC checks.
- Integrate onboarding systems with BVN/NIN databases through secure APIs.
- Enable dynamic risk scoring based on KYC results.
- Store all identity verification logs for audit trail and compliance review.
controls.additionalControl:
- Implement fallback manual verification in cases of BVN/NIN service downtime.
- Periodic penetration testing and system audit to verify integrity of integrations.
- Set up alerts for onboarding anomalies, such as multiple applications from same identity.
controls.responsibilityText: - Chief Compliance Officer - Head of Onboarding/KYC Unit - IT/Technology Integration Lead - AML Systems Analyst
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Digital Banking/Onboarding Team - Regulatory Compliance Officer - Cybersecurity Unit
controls.reason: Primary responsibility text lists Chief Compliance Officer, Head of Onboarding/KYC Unit, IT/Technology Integration Lead, and AML Systems Analyst. The CCO is accountable for CDD/KYC, with IT and onboarding as contributors. Internal Audit verifies through periodic audits.

controls.title: Enforcement & Compliance Monitoring
controls.control:
- Conduct quarterly internal reviews to ensure AML systems meet baseline standards.
- Maintain an evidence-based compliance register.
- Submit regulatory self-assessment reports.
- Ensure board oversight on AML compliance.
controls.additionalControl:
- Engage external independent audit annually to assess AML system compliance.
- Train staff on updated CBN expectations.
- Maintain a compliance dashboard with real-time reporting to executive management.
controls.responsibilityText: - Chief Compliance Officer - Head, Internal Audit - Risk & Control Department - IT Governance & Strategy Lead
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Compliance Monitoring Team - Board Audit Committee - Chief Risk Officer
controls.reason: Primary responsibility text includes Chief Compliance Officer, Head of Internal Audit, Risk & Control Department, and IT Governance & Strategy Lead. The CCO is accountable for enforcement and compliance monitoring, with Internal Audit, Risk, and IT as contributors. Internal Audit also verifies independently.

controls.title: Other Requirements
controls.control:
- Maintain a comprehensive AML System Register submitted to CBN.
- Develop and implement a Vendor Management Policy.
- Include compliance clauses in all third-party contracts.
- Periodically assess third-party AML compliance.
controls.additionalControl:
- Conduct annual third-party audits on AML service providers.
- Use Service Level Agreements (SLAs) with penalties for non-compliance.
- Include regulatory compliance checkpoints in vendor onboarding process.
controls.responsibilityText: - Chief Compliance Officer - Head, IT Strategy - Procurement/Vendor Management Lead - Legal & Regulatory Compliance Unit
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Compliance Department - Vendor Management Office - Risk Management Unit - Board Compliance Oversight Committee
controls.reason: Primary responsibility text lists Chief Compliance Officer, Head of IT Strategy, Procurement/Vendor Management Lead, and Legal & Regulatory Compliance Unit. The CCO is accountable for AML system register and vendor management policy, with IT, Procurement, and Legal as contributors. Internal Audit verifies through annual third-party audits.

controls.title: Implementation and Compliance
controls.control:
- Develop a compliance roadmap with milestones toward alignment.
- Conduct internal AML system gap analysis against baseline standards.
- Maintain a training calendar and LMS (Learning Management System) for AML staff.
- Submit periodic progress reports to CBN.
controls.additionalControl:
- Conduct mock regulatory inspections.
- Engage external consultants to validate AML system readiness.
- Incorporate training feedback loops to improve AML team capacity.
controls.responsibilityText: - Chief Compliance Officer - Head of AML Systems - Chief Risk Officer - HR Training & Development
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - AML Program Implementation Team - Compliance & Internal Audit - Regulatory Liaison Officer - Board AML Oversight Committee
controls.reason: Primary responsibility text includes Chief Compliance Officer, Head of AML Systems, Chief Risk Officer, and HR Training & Development. The CCO is accountable for implementation and compliance roadmap, with Risk and HR as contributors. Internal Audit verifies through mock inspections and reviews.

controls.act: Suspicious Transaction Reporting on United Nations Security Council Resolutions on Proliferation Financing
controls.title: Suspicious Transaction Reporting on United Nations Security Council Resolutions on Proliferation Financing
controls.control:
- Daily automated screening of customers and transactions against updated UN sanctions Lists
- Escalation protocol for potential or confirmed matches
- Prompt STR filing with NFIU and freezing of associated accounts
- Staff training on proliferation financing risks and red flags
controls.additionalControl:
- Subscribe to real-time sanctions list updates 
- Integrate proliferation financing risk into enterprise-wide risk assessment 
- Conduct periodic testing of screening systems for effectiveness and coverage

controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Head of AML/CFT Compliance, Head of Operations, IT/Sanctions List Management Officer
controls.reason: Primary responsibility text lists Chief Compliance Officer, Transaction Monitoring Team, and Sanctions Screening Unit. Internal Audit verifies through periodic testing.

controls.act: ECONOMIC AND FINANCIAL CRIMES COMMISSION (ESTABLISHMENT) ACT 2004
controls.title: Freezing Order on Banks or Other Financial Institutions
controls.control:

- Automated alert systems to flag EFCC directives.
- Training for branch managers and key officers on EFCC compliance.
- Maintain EFCC order compliance logs.
controls.additionalControl:

- Dedicated EFCC liaison desk at compliance unit.

controls.act: CBN Guidelines on Management of Dormant Accounts, Unclaimed Balances and Other Financial Assets

controls.control:

- Regular communication protocol with customers

- Quarterly dormant reporting workflow and tools

controls.additionalControl:

- Reconciliation checks before CBN transfer

controls.title: MANAGEMENT OF DORMANT ACCOUNTS AND UNCLAIMED FINANCIAL ASSETS
controls.control:

- Dual approval for account reactivation
- Dormant Accounts Register (system-based)
- Automated system flag for 10-year threshold accounts

- Regular audits on dormant account handling
- Escalation framework for delayed transfers
- Automated compliance tracking dashboard

controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Head of Compliance - Chief Risk Officer - Chief Financial Officer - Head, Operations Control
controls.reason: Primary responsibility lists Compliance Department, Branch Operations, Internal Control, Finance Department; additional lists Head of Compliance, CRO, CFO, Head Operations Control. Compliance Department is most accountable for dormant account management policy and register.

controls.title: RE-ACTIVATION OF DORMANT ACCOUNT
controls.control:
- Reactivation checklist and approval workflow
- Face-to-face identity verification
- Dual authorization
- TAT tracking system (3-day SLA)
- No charge flag in transaction system
controls.additionalControl:
- Audit trail of all reactivation approvals

controls.title: DISPUTE RESOULUTION
controls.control:
- Complaint resolution procedures aligned with CPR timelines
- Complaint management system with case tracking
- Clear display of complaint channels and escalation paths

- Staff training on dispute resolution procedures

controls.act: Guidelines on Operations of Bank Accounts for Virtual Assets Service Providers (VASPs)
controls.title: PERMISSIBLE ACTIVITIES
controls.control:
- Restrict activities strictly to those permitted by CBN
- Maintain a list of approved VASPs
- Implement transaction monitoring tools for VASP accounts
controls.additionalControl:
- Obtain written CBN approvals for any new activity
- Conduct periodic KYC/AML reviews on all VASP accounts
- Integrate risk scoring for VASP-related clients

controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Head, Compliance - Chief Risk Officer - Relationship Manager (VASPs)
controls.reason: Primary responsibility lists Head of Digital Banking, Operations Unit, Compliance Department; additional lists Head Compliance, CRO, Relationship Manager VASPs. Compliance/AML-CFT is most accountable for VASP permissible activity restrictions and monitoring.

controls.title: OPERATION OF BANK ACCOUNT BY VASPs
controls.control:
- Require and verify SEC licence before onboarding
- Conduct full CDD/KYC checks on directors and BOs
- Enforce internal approval workflows for account setup
- Monitor and report account activities to CBN monthly
- Implement use restrictions (no cash/cheques/FX from VASP accounts)
controls.additionalControl:
- Integrate AML transaction monitoring tools for VASP accounts
- Maintain live access to transaction logs on designated settlement accounts
- Automate dormant account detection and closure workflows
- Maintain collateral monitoring (150% rule) and settlement cycle enforcement (T+3)
controls.responsibilityText: - Head of Operations - Compliance Department - Legal & Documentation Unit - Risk Management Unit
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Chief Compliance Officer - Head, IT Systems (for API and real-time integration) - Relationship Managers for VASPs
controls.reason: Primary responsibility lists Head of Operations, Compliance Department, Legal & Documentation Unit, Risk Management Unit; additional lists Chief Compliance Officer, Head IT Systems, Relationship Managers. Compliance owns VASP account operation controls, with CCO accountable.

controls.title: RISK MANAGEMENT FOR ANTI-MONEY LAUNDERING, COMBATING THE FINANCING OF TERRORISM AND COUNTER PROLIFERATION FINANCING (AML, CFT, AND CPF)
controls.control:
- Implement automated CDD & EDD systems
- Daily transaction monitoring and flagging
- Validate customer information with national ID databases (NIN, BVN)
- File STRs promptly and maintain AML records for 5 years
- Conduct on-site account reviews and set usage limits
controls.additionalControl:

- Independent AML/CFT audits
- Training programs for frontline staff
- Segregated reporting channels for whistleblowers
- Periodic update of customer risk profiles

controls.reason: Primary responsibility lists Compliance Officer, AML/CFT Unit, Internal Audit, Relationship Managers, Risk Management; additional lists CCO, Head Financial Crimes Risk, AML Analysts, IT/Data Governance. AML/CFT Unit is most accountable for AML/CFT/CPF controls.

controls.title: CONSUMER PROTECTION MEASURES
controls.control:
- Implement fraud detection systems on designated accounts
- Provide toll-free numbers, emails, and online portals for complaints
- Integrate with CBN CCMS
- Train staff on complaints handling procedures and timelines
- Maintain complaint logs and resolution reports
controls.additionalControl:
- Real-time complaint tracking dashboard
- Automated escalation protocols for unresolved complaints
- Customer satisfaction surveys after complaint closure
- Quarterly reviews of complaint data and fraud trends

controls.reason: Primary responsibility lists Head Customer Service, Compliance Officer, Consumer Protection Unit, IT Department; additional lists Head Customer Experience, CCO, Consumer Protection Desk, Internal Audit. Consumer protection measures sit under Compliance/Conduct & Ethics, with Head of Compliance accountable.

controls.act: RE: Guidelines on Management of Dormant Accounts, Unclaimed Balances and Other Financial Assets in Banks and Other Financial Institutions in Nigeria
controls.title: FPR/DIR/PUB/CIR/001/004
controls.control: Internal data publishing policy; publication content vetting; annual dormant account disclosure schedule; NDPA compliance checklist.
controls.additionalControl: Legal review of content pre-publication; centralized publication approval process; staff training on lawful disclosures.

controls.reason: Responsibility text lists Legal, Compliance, Corporate Communications, IT; additional lists Compliance, Corporate Comms, Legal, IT. NDPA compliance and data publishing policy make Data Protection the most accountable unit, with DPO as role.

controls.act: Clean Note Policy Version 0.1
controls.title: Deposit of Banknotes by DMBs and CPCs at CBN
controls.control:
- Implement internal cash sorting and fitness checking procedures
- Use CBN-approved note processing equipment
- Train staff on the visual indicators of unfit/mutilated notes
- Package and label boxes strictly as per CBN requirements
controls.additionalControl:
- Periodic quality audits of sorted notes
- CCTV review of cash handling process
- Escalation process for rejected deposits
- Quarterly refresher training on banknote classification
controls.responsibilityText: - Head of Cash Operations - Branch Managers - Vault Supervisors - Head of Compliance - Designated officers interfacing with CPCs
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Operations Control Unit - Head of Cash Management - Compliance Department - Internal Audit (for spot checks)
controls.reason: Primary responsibility lists Head of Cash Operations, Branch Managers, Vault Supervisors, Head of Compliance, designated CPC officers; additional lists Operations Control, Head of Cash Management, Compliance, Internal Audit. Cash Management owns banknote deposit and sorting controls.

controls.title: Re-Circulation of Banknotes by DMBs and CPCs
controls.control:
- Deploy only approved and calibrated sorting machines.
- Enforce mandatory processing and classification of all notes.
- Implement dual verification of cash sorting results.
- Regularly train staff on CBN fitness parameters and update them on test pack changes.
- Random audit checks on ATM and OTC notes.
controls.additionalControl:
- Integrate automated monitoring and audit logs for cash sorting machines.
- Conduct monthly internal reviews of notes dispensed through ATMs and counters.
- Establish a penalty recovery process for branches that breach note standards.
controls.responsibilityText: - Cash Operations Team - Vault Custodians - ATM Maintenance Teams - Compliance & Risk Units - Branch Operations Managers
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Head of Cash Operations - Chief Compliance Officer - Internal Audit Unit - IT Support (for machine configuration logs)
controls.reason: Primary responsibility lists Cash Operations Team, Vault Custodians, ATM Maintenance Teams, Compliance & Risk Units, Branch Operations Managers; additional lists Head of Cash Operations, CCO, Internal Audit, IT Support. Cash Management owns banknote recirculation controls.

controls.title: Machines Eligible for Currency Processing in the Industry
controls.control:
- Maintain an inventory of all currency processing machines.
- Ensure machines are certified and verified by the CBN.
- Conduct regular calibration and testing based on CBN’s test pack standards.
- Maintain a record of CBN approvals and machine adaptation history.
controls.additionalControl:
- Establish a CBN liaison officer to track machine compliance updates.
- Vendor agreements must include obligation for periodic upgrades to align with CBN standards.
- Include machine conformity checks as part of internal and external audits.
controls.responsibilityText: - Head of Operations - Cash Management Team - IT & Equipment Procurement Unit - Compliance and Internal Control Unit
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Head of Procurement & Equipment - Head of Operations - Chief Compliance Officer - CBN Monitoring Desk Liaison
controls.reason: Head of Operations is the most accountable for maintaining currency processing machines, with cash management, IT/procurement, and compliance/internal control as contributors. Internal Audit independently verifies.

controls.title: Automated Teller Machines (ATMs)
controls.control:
- Ensure ATMs are loaded only with authenticated and fitness-checked notes.
- Conduct routine testing and servicing of ATM sensors for counterfeit detection.
- Use certified sorting machines before ATM loading.
- Maintain an audit trail of cash loading and source of notes.
controls.additionalControl:
- Integrate real-time ATM monitoring for note rejection or customer complaints.
- Periodically retrain ATM custodians and cash handlers.
- Introduce mystery shopping exercises to detect breaches.
- Include ATM note quality check in internal audit scope.
controls.responsibilityText: - Head of ATM Operations - Cash Management/Branch Operations Team - IT Infrastructure Unit - Compliance Unit
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - ATM Service Manager - Operations Risk Officer - Internal Audit Team - Compliance/CBN Liaison Desk
controls.reason: ATM operations fall under Operations; Head of Operations is accountable. Contributors include cash management, IT, and compliance. Internal Audit verifies.

controls.title: Counterfeit Notes Discovered
controls.control:
- Train staff on currency authentication techniques.
- Use CBN-approved currency processing machines with counterfeit detection features.
- Establish a standard operating procedure (SOP) for handling and forwarding counterfeit notes.
- Log and maintain records of all counterfeit incidents.
controls.additionalControl:
- Conduct random reviews of branch-level currency transactions.
- Establish a central counterfeit reporting log across branches.
- Ensure counterfeit notes are tagged with relevant incident reports and forwarded to CBN within stipulated time.
- Include counterfeit incident reporting in audit reviews.
controls.responsibilityText: - Branch Operations Manager - Cash & Treasury Management Team - Internal Control Officer - Compliance Department
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Cash Officers - Operations Risk Manager - Internal Audit Team - CBN Compliance Liaison
controls.reason: Branch Operations Manager is accountable for counterfeit note handling at branch level. Contributors include cash/treasury, internal control, and compliance. Internal Audit verifies.

controls.title: Mutilated Banknotes Management
controls.control:
- Train branch staff on CBN-approved mutilated note handling procedures.
- Maintain a copy of the CBN Operational Manual at all cash-handling branches.
- Use special handling forms and reporting templates for all such transactions.
- Keep proper documentation and audit trail for every mutilated note received or replaced.
controls.additionalControl:
- Schedule periodic refresher training on handling of mutilated notes.
- Perform surprise audits on branches' mutilated notes management processes.
- Integrate mutilated note processing into internal audit scope.
controls.responsibilityText: - Branch Operations Manager - Cash Officers / Tellers - Treasury Department - Compliance Unit
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Head of Operations - Cash Management Unit - Audit & Internal Control
controls.reason: Branch Operations Manager is accountable for mutilated note management. Contributors include cash officers, treasury, and compliance. Internal Audit verifies.

controls.title: Publicity Campaign
controls.control:
- Integrate CBN sensitization themes in internal campaigns and customer touchpoints.
- Train frontline staff on clean note policy and security features of genuine notes.
- Monitor and prevent issuance of unfit or dirty notes from ATMs and counters.
- Display anti-naira abuse messages in banking halls and on digital platforms.
controls.additionalControl:
- Partner with CBN in joint customer engagement activities.
- Publish quarterly updates on clean note initiatives and performance.
- Use educational infographics in branches and ATMs.
controls.responsibilityText: - Corporate Communications Unit - Operations Department - Branch Operations Managers - Compliance Department
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Head of Corporate Affairs/Communication - Customer Service Management Team - Cash Management Unit
controls.reason: Publicity campaign for clean note policy is primarily an operations/customer-facing responsibility. Head of Operations is accountable. Compliance verifies.

controls.control:
- Use CBN-approved cash processing machines that verify authenticity.
- Implement regular fitness sorting and counterfeit detection protocols.
- Conduct routine spot testing of ATM dispensed notes.
- Train staff and custodians on CBN's Clean Note Policy.
controls.additionalControl:
- Conduct internal ATM inspections weekly.
- Introduce mystery shopper checks for teller cash quality.
- Keep a log of ATM/teller cash sorting dates and quality certifications.

controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Head of Operations & Technology - Head of Cash & Treasury - Compliance & Risk Units

controls.act: Updated Penalty on Inappropriate Cash Disbursement Practices by Deposit Money Banks (DMBs)

controls.control:
- Implement dual authorization for all disbursements of mint notes.
- Maintain detailed logs of mint note inflows and disbursement.
- Conduct internal surveillance of teller and vault operations.
- Limit mint notes to customer-requested withdrawals only.
controls.additionalControl:
- Deploy CCTV and biometric access controls at cash centres.
- Carry out mystery shopper testing internally to assess adherence.
- Train staff on legal implications and ethics around mint note handling.
controls.responsibilityText: - Head of Cash Management - Branch Managers - Teller Supervisors - Internal Control & Audit Units
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - COO/Head of Operations - Cash Management Department - Internal Audit/Compliance Units
controls.reason: Head of Cash Management is accountable for mint note disbursement practices. Internal Audit verifies.

controls.act: Treatment of Composed Banknotes
controls.title: COD/DIR/INT/CIR/001/006
controls.control:
- Use CBN-approved cash sorting machines with image sensors to detect composed notes.
- Ensure manual verification by trained staff for doubtful notes.
- Maintain segregated logs for suspected mutilated or composed notes.
controls.additionalControl:
- Conduct training for cash handlers on identifying composed notes.
- Sample-check deposits before dispatch to CBN.
- Implement pre-deposit audit checks for all boxes of notes.

controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Cash Processing Officers - Head of Operations - Compliance & Internal Control Unit
controls.reason: Head of Cash Operations is accountable for composed banknote treatment. Internal Audit verifies.

controls.act: Nigerian Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC) Act, 2023
controls.title: Participating Financial Institutions
controls.control:
- Ensure all deposit products are registered with the NDIC.
- Timely remittance of NDIC premiums.

controls.responsibilityText: - Legal and Compliance Department- Product Management Team- Customer Experience/Service Department- Marketing and Sales Team- IT/Business Process Automation Team
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Chief Compliance Officer- Head, Legal and Regulatory Affairs- Head, Customer Experience- Head, Products- Head, Digital Channels/IT
controls.reason: Consumer Protection Compliance Policy, standardized literature and complaints framework are compliance-owned; the Chief Compliance Officer is named. Internal Audit performs internal audits and compliance self-assessments.

controls.title: RESPONSIBLE LENDING
controls.control:
- Incorporate responsible lending checks into credit policy and procedures.
- Embed income and affordability checks in loan application systems.
- Set automated CRMS and credit bureau validation before approval.
- Develop SOPs for handling financial difficulty cases.
- Train staff on third-party product disclosure rules.
- Require written declarations and advice confirmations from guarantors.
- Automate alerts for periodic loan performance updates to guarantors.
- Automate discharge letter issuance within 5 business days.
controls.additionalControl:
- Quarterly audits of loan files to check compliance with responsible lending requirements.
- Review of system logs for CRMS/bureau checks.
- Periodic staff training on loan suitability, disclosures, and guarantor rights.
- Internal compliance reviews of customer notification practices (declined loans, discharge letters, etc.).
controls.responsibilityText: - Credit Risk Management Unit- Loan Approval Officers- Legal and Compliance Department- Customer Service/Experience- Loan Monitoring/Collections Team
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Chief Compliance Officer- Head of Credit Risk- Head, Collections & Monitoring- Head of Legal- Head of Customer Experience
controls.reason: Responsible lending checks, affordability and CRMS/bureau validation are credit-risk controls owned by Risk Management (Credit Risk); Compliance and Legal are contributors. Internal Audit performs quarterly loan-file audits.

controls.title: SALES PROMOTION
controls.control:
- Implement a compliance review process for all advertisements and promotions.
- Develop and deliver regular training for all marketing and sales staff.
- Enforce a code of ethics for marketing and sales.
- Conduct regular performance assessments and competency reviews of staff.
- Design a balanced scorecard for sales incentives that includes customer satisfaction.
- Include opt-out options clearly in all promotional messages (SMS, emails, etc.).
controls.additionalControl:
- Periodic mystery shopper tests to verify ethical sales behavior.
- Maintain an audit trail for customer opt-out requests.
- Include pre-approval from Compliance before running any major sales promotion.
- Establish feedback loops for customer reactions to marketing campaigns.
- Include disclosure reviews in internal audit programs.
controls.responsibilityText: - Head of Marketing- Head of Compliance- Head of Human Resources- Sales and Product Teams- Customer Experience/Service Team
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Chief Compliance Officer- Head of Sales/Marketing- Head of Internal Audit- Head of Learning & Development
controls.reason: Sales promotion compliance review, ethics code and opt-out enforcement are compliance-owned; the Chief Compliance Officer is named. Marketing, HR and Sales are contributors. Internal Audit includes disclosure reviews in its programs.

controls.title: DATA PROTECTION AND PRIVACY
controls.control:
- Data Protection & Privacy Policy (aligned with NDPA/NDPR).
- Consent forms embedded in digital/onboarding journeys.
- Encryption, firewalls, and access control protocols.
- Periodic internal audits on data access logs.
- Customer communication protocols and records.
- Data quality and KYC validation processes.
controls.additionalControl:
- Implement automated data consent dashboards (opt-in/opt-out history).- Consent renewal prompts at intervals.
- Data sharing logs with customer alerts.- Staff training on data privacy & compliance.
- Real-time update validation for critical customer data (e.g., email, phone).
- Periodic compliance reviews with NDPA/CBN standards.
controls.responsibilityText: - Data Protection Officer (DPO)- IT Security- Compliance & Legal- Customer Service- Operations- Digital Channels / CRM Team
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Data Protection Officer (DPO), Head of IT Security, Head of Compliance, Customer Experience Lead, Legal Department
controls.reason: Data protection and privacy policy, consent and NDPA/NDPR alignment are owned by the Data Protection Officer within Compliance (Data Protection); IT Security, Legal and Operations are contributors. Internal Audit performs periodic audits on data access logs.

controls.title: GENERAL PROVISIONS
controls.control:
- Complaint Management Policy (documented and approved).
- Dedicated complaints handling unit with escalation matrix.
- CRM system for tracking and resolving complaints.
- Complaint channels published on websites, mobile apps, branches.
- Periodic staff training on dispute resolution protocols.
controls.additionalControl:
- Publish complaint resolution SLAs (e.g., 5–10 business days) visibly across channels.
- Auto-acknowledgement system when complaints are lodged.
- Monthly review of complaint trends and escalations.
- Regular training updates for complaint handling staff.
- Internal audit review of complaint resolution performance.
controls.responsibilityText: - Customer Service / Customer Experience Team- Compliance Team- Branch Managers- Contact Center Managers- IT / Digital Channels Team
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Head of Customer Experience, Compliance Officer, Contact Center Lead, Head of Digital Channels, Internal Control Unit
controls.reason: Complaint management is operationally owned by Customer Service under Operations; Head of Operations is the accountable role. Compliance and IT are contributors. Internal Audit verifies complaint resolution performance.

controls.title: COMPLAINTS MANAGEMENT CHANNELS
controls.control:
- Multiple complaint channels (email, SMS, call centers, social media, branch desks).
- CRM or ticketing system that logs and tracks complaints.
- Acknowledgement templates for complaint response.
- Fraud hotlines available 24/7.
- Complaint SOP (Standard Operating Procedures).
controls.additionalControl:
- Enforce automatic ID and 24-hour acknowledgment for every complaint.
- Track and test functionality of complaint channels weekly.
- Develop escalation framework for emergency fraud-related complaints.
- Train frontline staff on handling complaints from vulnerable persons.
- Audit all complaint systems for uptime and accessibility.
controls.responsibilityText: - Customer Service/Experience Department- IT Department (Digital Platforms)- Contact Center Operations- Social Media/Communications Team- Compliance Unit
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Head of Customer Experience, IT Support Manager, Head of Contact Center, Fraud Risk Manager, Head of Compliance
controls.reason: Complaint channels are primarily managed by Customer Service/Experience; Head of Operations is accountable. IT, Contact Center, and Compliance are contributors. Internal Audit audits complaint systems.

controls.title: INTERNAL DISPUTE RESOLUTION
controls.control:
- Develop and maintain a formal IDR policy.
- Automate complaint logging and tracking system with timestamped acknowledgment.
- Assign dedicated complaint handling officers with SLAs.
- Implement workflow alerts to ensure timely escalation and response.
- Regular training for staff on customer complaint handling.
- Set up a central complaint database for monitoring resolution timelines.
controls.additionalControl:
- Regular internal audit of complaint handling process.
- Periodic reporting to executive management on IDR performance.
- Feedback surveys to monitor customer satisfaction with complaint resolution.
- Incorporate compliance KPIs into staff performance metrics.
controls.responsibilityText: - Executive Compliance Officer- Customer Experience/Service Team- Head of Operations- IT/Complaint Management System Administrator
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Chief Compliance Officer (Oversight)- Complaint Resolution Team Lead (Execution)- IT Head (System Support)- Internal Audit (Monitoring & Evaluation)
controls.reason: Internal Dispute Resolution policy and oversight are compliance-owned; Chief Compliance Officer is accountable. Customer Service and IT execute. Internal Audit monitors and evaluates.

controls.title: COMPLIANCE
controls.control:
- Compliance Unit established
- Regulatory Monitoring Function in place
- General policies on regulatory compliance exist
- Board policy review calendar maintained
controls.additionalControl:
- Draft a standalone Consumer Protection Compliance Policy immediately if not already in place
- Present draft to Management Committee, then to Board for approval
- Ensure policy includes alignment with all sections of the Regulation (Equity, Disclosure, Redress, Privacy, etc.)
- Schedule annual policy review to update based on new CBN directives
controls.responsibilityText: - Head of Compliance- Legal Department- Company Secretary- Head of Risk Management- Board of Directors
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Head of Compliance, Company Secretary, Risk & Control, Board Governance Team
controls.reason: Consumer protection compliance policy is owned by Compliance; Head of Compliance is accountable. Legal, Company Secretariat, Risk, and Board are contributors. Internal Audit verifies.

controls.act: Cybercrime (Prohibition, Prevention, Etc) Act, Amendment 2024
controls.title: Exceptions to Financial Institutions posting and authorized posting options.
controls.control:
- Enforce segregation of duties in transaction workflows.
- Deploy dual-authentication systems for transaction posting and authorization.
- Implement real-time fraud monitoring systems.
- Carry out periodic security audits and access reviews.
- Conduct employee training on cyber risk awareness and information security.
controls.additionalControl:
- Include automated alert systems for unusual account activity.
- Engage external penetration testing consultants.
- Maintain a fraud incident response protocol.
- Require compliance sign-off on access control settings.
controls.responsibilityText: - Head of Operations- Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)- Compliance Officer- Internal Control Unit
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Chief Compliance Officer- CISO- Head of Internal Audit- Head of IT Security
controls.reason: Cybercrime Act transaction security controls are owned by IT Security under the CISO. Operations and Compliance contribute. Internal Audit verifies.

controls.title: Reporting Cyber Threats
controls.control:
- Establish a Cyber Incident Response Plan aligned with National CERT protocols.
- Maintain an updated communication flowchart for threat reporting.
- Train IT and security staff to identify and escalate threats immediately.
- Set up real-time threat detection systems integrated with SOC/CERT frameworks.
controls.additionalControl:
- Schedule periodic simulations and drills involving threat reporting to CERT.
- Engage with industry CERT coordination workshops and updates.
- Audit and review compliance with incident reporting SOPs.
- Automate CERT notification triggers within the threat management system.
controls.responsibilityText: - Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)- Head of IT Security- Head of Risk Management- Chief Compliance Officer
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - CISO- Compliance Officer- Head of IT- SOC Team Lead
controls.reason: Cyber threat reporting and CERT protocols are owned by IT Security under the CISO. Risk and Compliance contribute. Internal Audit audits incident reporting SOPs.

controls.title: Electronic Cards Related Fraud.
controls.control:
- Only engage with licensed Credit Bureaus approved by regulators.
- Obtain explicit consent from customers before any data sharing.
- Implement data protection policies aligned with NDPR and NITDA rules.
- Document and track all disclosures of cardholder data.
- Ensure timely notification to cardholders within the 7-day window via email/SMS or other agreed means.
controls.additionalControl:
- Conduct periodic audits of data access and disclosures.
- Maintain a data-sharing register with timestamps and disclosure recipients.
- Implement automated alert systems for disclosure deadlines.
- Regular staff training on data privacy compliance and obligations under this section.
controls.responsibilityText: - Chief Compliance Officer- Head of Data Protection/Privacy- Head of Cards Operations- Legal and Regulatory Affairs Department
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Data Protection Officer (DPO)- Compliance Officer- Head of Cards- Legal Department
controls.reason: Cardholder data protection and NDPR compliance are owned by Data Protection under the DPO. Cards Operations and Legal contribute. Internal Audit audits data access and disclosures.

controls.title: Duties of Financial Institutions.
controls.control:
- Enforce mandatory NIN collection at point of card issuance.
- Conduct KYC checks (name, address, ID) during customer onboarding.
- Implement automated identity verification systems (e.g., NIMC API integration).
- Maintain secure documentation and storage of all KYC information.
- Integrate KYC checks before electronic transfer or debit order execution.
controls.additionalControl:
- Periodic internal audits of account opening and KYC procedures.
- Enable KYC review alerts for expiring documents or missing data.
- Conduct staff training on identity verification and fraud prevention.
- Implement data validation tools and 2FA for electronic transactions.
controls.responsibilityText: - Head of Operations- Chief Compliance Officer- Head of Risk Management- Customer Service/Account Opening Unit- Head of e-Channels/Card Services
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Chief Compliance Officer- Head of Customer Experience- Data Protection Officer- Head of e-Banking- Head of Internal Audit
controls.reason: KYC and NIN collection duties are compliance-owned under AML/CFT; Chief Compliance Officer is accountable. Operations and Customer Service execute. Internal Audit verifies.

controls.title: Records Retention and Protection of Data
controls.control:
- Implement automated data retention systems with access logs and secure backups.
- Ensure strict access controls and encryption on retained data.
- Maintain policies for responding to law enforcement and regulator requests.
- Align retention and disclosure practices with NDPC and NCC guidelines.
controls.additionalControl:
- Conduct quarterly audits of data retention and disclosure logs.
- Develop a centralized request management system with escalation protocols.
- Run mock drills and compliance testing to simulate real data disclosure scenarios.
controls.responsibilityText: - Chief Information Officer (CIO) - Chief Compliance Officer (CCO) - Data Protection Officer (DPO)
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - DPO for data privacy compliance - Head of IT Security for technical safeguards - Compliance Monitoring Unit for oversight
controls.reason: Records retention and data protection are owned by Data Protection under the DPO. IT Security provides technical safeguards. Internal Audit conducts quarterly audits.

controls.title: Failure of Service Providers to perform certain duties
controls.control:
- Maintain up-to-date Cybercrime Act compliance procedures.
- Establish Law Enforcement Liaison Desk or protocol.
- Maintain secure records to support investigations.
- Integrate cybercrime intelligence sharing procedures.
- Create internal Service Suspension/Deactivation Policy aligned with legal requests.
controls.additionalControl:
- Train staff on handling law enforcement requests compliantly.
- Set up audit trails for information shared or services deactivated.
- Include cybercrime support clauses in vendor/service contracts.
- Periodically review and test procedures for responsiveness.
controls.responsibilityText: - Chief Compliance Officer (CCO) - Chief Legal Officer (CLO) - Head of IT/Security - DPO (for data privacy intersections)
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Compliance Unit for process governance - Legal for response authorization - IT/Security for execution and logs management
controls.reason: Service provider cybercrime compliance procedures are compliance-owned; CCO is accountable. Legal authorizes responses and IT executes. Internal Audit verifies.

controls.act: Issuance of Risk-Based Cybersecurity Framework and Guidelines for Deposit Money Banks and Payment Service Providers
controls.title: Cybersecurity Programme
controls.control:
- Implement all 9 components listed in the guideline
- Regularly update cybersecurity risk assessments
- Establish a formal Incident Response Plan (IRP)
- Conduct periodic vulnerability scans and penetration tests
- Maintain real-time log monitoring and alerts
- Enforce a routine backup/recovery strategy
- Run quarterly security awareness trainings
- Monitor and report on cybersecurity maturity improvement
- Track key metrics (e.g., time to detect/respond to incidents)
controls.additionalControl:
- Conduct independent cybersecurity audits
- Benchmark against NIST or ISO 27001 frameworks
- Automate threat detection and response (SIEM, SOAR tools)
- Include Board-level oversight for cybersecurity risk posture
- Integrate cyber risk metrics into Enterprise Risk Management (ERM)
controls.responsibilityText: - Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) - Chief Compliance Officer (CCO) - Head of IT Risk - Cybersecurity Programme Manager
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - IT Security and Risk Departments - Compliance for governance oversight - Internal Audit for monitoring effectiveness
controls.reason: Cybersecurity programme is owned by IT Security under the CISO. Compliance provides governance oversight. Internal Audit independently audits effectiveness.

controls.title: Other Risk Management Control Functions
controls.control:
- Implement formal and structured risk assessment tools and methodologies.
- Submit monthly reports to Senior Management and quarterly to the Board Risk Committee.
- Conduct periodic independent cybersecurity audits.
- Verify qualifications of all audit, risk, and compliance staff or consultants.
- Maintain clearly defined cybersecurity audit scope and periodic compliance reviews.
controls.additionalControl:
- Deploy automated dashboards for risk metrics and tracking.
- Engage external cybersecurity auditors at regular intervals.
- Provide regular training and certification for staff in risk, audit, and compliance functions.
- Ensure active involvement of Board-level oversight in cybersecurity governance.
controls.responsibilityText: - Head of Risk Management - Head of Internal Audit - Chief Compliance Officer - Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) - Board Risk Management Committee - Senior Management
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - CISO - Heads of Risk, Audit, and Compliance - Board Risk Management Committee - Senior Management
contributors: Heads of Risk, Audit, and Compliance
controls.reason: Other risk management control functions are owned by Risk Management under Head of Risk. Internal Audit, Compliance, and CISO contribute. Internal Audit verifies.

controls.title: The Risk Management System
controls.control:
- Maintain a risk register identifying threats and vulnerabilities.
- Perform and document Cybersecurity Risk Control Self-Assessments.
- Ensure annual and change-triggered risk assessments.
- Establish Board-approved risk acceptance criteria.
- Maintain audit-reviewed risk assessment methodology.
- Maintain documentation for risk treatment decisions (e.g., acceptance, transfer).
controls.additionalControl:
- Use automated risk assessment tools.
- Implement scenario-based testing and simulation exercises.
- Conduct quarterly mini-risk reviews in addition to annual assessments.
- Train all relevant staff on enterprise risk management and treatment strategies.
- Link risk treatment plans directly to the SFI’s cybersecurity roadmap and business continuity plans.
controls.responsibilityText: - Chief Risk Officer (CRO) - Chief Compliance Officer (CCO) - Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) - Head of Internal Audit - Board Risk Management Committee
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - CISO - CRO - Head of Audit - Risk Management Unit - Board Risk Management Committee
controls.reason: The CRO is listed first and is the most accountable for maintaining the risk management system, including the risk register and risk assessments. The CCO, CISO, Head of Internal Audit, and Board Risk Management Committee are contributors. Internal Audit provides independent verification.

controls.title: Vulnerability Identification
controls.control:
- Maintain a yearly calendar for third-party-led vulnerability assessments.
- Automate internal scans with up-to-date scanning tools.
- Document vulnerabilities, assign remediation tasks, and track closure.
- Store scan results and remediation logs for audit purposes.
controls.additionalControl:
- Incorporate threat intelligence feeds into scan tools.
- Conduct red team/blue team exercises.
- Submit quarterly scan summary to the Board Risk Committee.
controls.reason: The CISO is explicitly named as primarily responsible for vulnerability identification, including maintaining the assessment calendar and scans. The Head of IT Risk & Governance and the Information Security & Risk Management Department are contributors. Internal Audit verifies.

controls.title: Third party risk management
controls.control:
- Implement formal TPRM framework with documented procedures.
- Enforce due diligence checklists and third-party risk ratings.
- Maintain central register of all contracts and SLAs.
- Schedule periodic vendor performance reviews and audits.
- Conduct annual cybersecurity training for critical third parties.
- Include business continuity clauses in vendor agreements.
- Review insurance policies annually for adequacy.
controls.additionalControl:
- Include right-to-audit and breach notification clauses in all contracts.
- Automate third-party onboarding and monitoring via TPRM tools.
- Report third-party risk trends to the Risk Management Committee.
controls.responsibilityText: - Head, Procurement - Head, IT Risk & Information Security - Legal & Compliance Unit
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Enterprise Risk Management / Vendor Management Unit / Information Security
controls.reason: The Head of Procurement is listed first and is most accountable for third-party risk management, including due diligence and contracts. However, the org structure lacks a dedicated Procurement unit under Finance & Treasury; Trade Services is the closest fit for vendor management. Contributors include IT Risk, Legal & Compliance, and others. Compliance verifies. Confidence is moderate due to ambiguity in unit mapping.

controls.title: Cybersecurity Maturity Assessment
controls.control:
- Use of the CBN Cybersecurity Self-Assessment Tool (CSAT)
- Periodic internal cybersecurity audits
- Management review of cyber maturity reports
- Integration of cyber roadmap into corporate strategy
controls.additionalControl:
- Independent validation of CSAT results
- Continuous maturity monitoring dashboard
- Third-party cybersecurity benchmarking
controls.responsibilityText: Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) / Cybersecurity Lead
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: CISO / Risk & Compliance Unit / IT Governance
controls.reason: The CISO is explicitly named as primarily responsible for cybersecurity maturity assessment. Contributors include the Cybersecurity Lead, Risk & Compliance Unit, and IT Governance. Internal Audit provides independent validation.

controls.title: Enhancing Cybersecurity Resilience
controls.control:
- Maintain real-time asset inventory tools and auditing schedules
- Enforce layered security controls (firewalls, encryption, access control)
- Use SIEM solutions and external SOC support where needed
- Maintain an Incident Response Plan (IRP) and CSIRT or retainer with external experts
- Participate in industry drills and simulate cyber scenarios internally
controls.additionalControl:
- Automate asset discovery and unauthorized access alerts
- Integrate AI-driven anomaly detection
- Conduct frequent control effectiveness reviews
- Share insights and best practices from sector exercises
controls.responsibilityText: - IT & Cybersecurity Team - Risk & Compliance Officer - Incident Response Team
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - CIO/Head of IT - Chief Compliance Officer - Cybersecurity Manager - Risk & Strategy Lead
controls.reason: The IT & Cybersecurity Team is listed first, but the CISO is the most accountable role for cybersecurity resilience. Contributors include the IT team, Risk & Compliance Officer, Incident Response Team, and others. Internal Audit verifies.

controls.title: Open Banking
controls.control:
- Enforce strong API access control (authentication, authorization, encryption)
- Conduct regular API vulnerability assessments and penetration testing
- Apply data minimization and anonymization for customer data
- Ensure customer consent management systems are implemented
- Align internal processes with Open Banking regulations and train staff accordingly
controls.additionalControl:
- Enforce strong API access control (authentication, authorization, encryption)
- Conduct regular API vulnerability assessments and penetration testing
- Apply data minimization and anonymization for customer data
- Ensure customer consent management systems are implemented
- Align internal processes with Open Banking regulations and train staff accordingly
controls.responsibilityText: - Chief Information Officer (CIO) - Chief Compliance Officer - API Management Team - IT Security Team
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - CIO/Head of IT - Head of Digital Banking - Chief Compliance Officer - Cybersecurity Manager
controls.reason: The CIO is listed first, but the CISO is more directly accountable for API security controls. Contributors include the CIO, CCO, API Management Team, and IT Security Team. Compliance verifies. Confidence is moderate due to competing accountability between CIO and CISO.

controls.title: Adoption of Emerging Technology
controls.control:
- Establish a technology governance committee to review and approve innovations.
- Implement a regulatory approval checklist for new tech deployments.
- Conduct sanctions screening on vendors, partners, and geographies before deployment.
- Vet APIs and third-party providers for CBN licensing status.
- Include risk assessments and regulatory compliance reviews in all innovation processes.
controls.additionalControl:
- Integrate automated sanction list screening tools.
- Schedule compliance reviews for all ongoing tech partnerships.
- Maintain audit trails of regulatory approvals and API access permissions.
- Implement emerging tech sandbox/testing environments to assess risks before full deployment.
controls.responsibilityText: - Chief Compliance Officer - Chief Technology Officer (CTO) - Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) - Head of Risk Management
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - CTO (Tech deployment approvals) - CCO (Regulatory compliance) - Vendor Management Lead (Third-party due diligence) - Internal Audit (Monitoring and assurance)
controls.reason: The CCO is listed first and is most accountable for regulatory compliance aspects of emerging technology adoption, including sanctions screening and regulatory checklists. Contributors include the CTO, CISO, Head of Risk Management, and Vendor Management Lead. Internal Audit verifies.

controls.title: Metrics, Monitoring and Reporting
controls.control:
- Establish and maintain performance dashboards tracking KPIs/KRIs.
- Schedule annual metric reviews and update as needed.
- Use employee portals or emails to circulate cybersecurity obligations.
- Adopt standardised reporting templates for quarterly board updates.
- Maintain an Incident Response Plan with notification protocols to CBN.
controls.additionalControl:
- Implement automated cyber performance reporting tools.
- Schedule quarterly cybersecurity training/awareness sessions.
- Define SOPs for timely cyber incident escalation and CBN reporting.
controls.responsibilityText: - Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) - Cybersecurity Risk Officer - Head of Compliance - Internal Audit - IT Security Department - Board Secretariat
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - CISO - Cybersecurity Risk Lead - Head of Compliance - Company Secretary - IT Security Lead
controls.reason: The CISO is listed first and is most accountable for metrics, monitoring, and reporting of cybersecurity performance. Contributors include the Cybersecurity Risk Officer, Head of Compliance, and others. Internal Audit verifies.

controls.title: Compliance with Statutory and Regulatory Requirements
controls.control:
- Maintain a compliance checklist covering key laws and CBN circulars.
- Appoint a regulatory liaison officer for CBN/NigFinCERT communication.
- Enrol in annual cyber drills and maintain attendance records.
- Periodically review alignment with NDPA and national policies.
controls.additionalControl:
- Subscribe to CBN/NigFinCERT bulletins for updated requirements.
- Conduct internal cyber incident simulations quarterly.
- Include regulatory compliance in internal audit scope.
controls.responsibilityText: - Board of Directors - Managing Director/CEO - Chief Compliance Officer - Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) - Legal and Regulatory Compliance Team - Cybersecurity Risk Officer
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Chief Compliance Officer - CISO - Legal Adviser - Internal Audit Head - Board Risk Committee Secretary
controls.reason: The CCO is explicitly named as primarily responsible for compliance with statutory and regulatory requirements, including maintaining the compliance checklist and regulatory liaison. Contributors include the Board, CEO, CISO, and others. Internal Audit verifies.

controls.title: SALES PROMOTION

- Periodic mystery shopper tests to verify ethical sales behavior.
- Maintain an audit trail for customer opt-out requests.

- Include disclosure reviews in internal audit programs.

controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Chief Compliance Officer- Head of Sales/Marketing- Head of Internal Audit- Head of Learning & Development
controls.reason: Compliance is accountable for sales promotion compliance and ethics; marketing, HR, sales, and customer experience are contributors. Internal Audit verifies via audit programs.

controls.title: DATA PROTECTION AND PRIVACY

- Consent forms embedded in digital/onboarding journeys.

- Customer communication protocols and records.
- Data quality and KYC validation processes.

controls.reason: Data Protection Officer is accountable for data protection and privacy; IT security, legal, customer service, operations, and digital channels are contributors. Internal Audit verifies via periodic audits.

controls.title: GENERAL PROVISIONS
controls.control:

- Internal audit review of complaint resolution performance.

controls.title: COMPLAINTS MANAGEMENT CHANNELS
controls.control:

controls.additionalControl:

- Train frontline staff on handling complaints from vulnerable persons.
- Audit all complaint systems for uptime and accessibility.
controls.responsibilityText: - Customer Service/Experience Department- IT Department (Digital Platforms)- Contact Center Operations- Social Media/Communications Team- Compliance Unit
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Head of Customer Experience, IT Support Manager, Head of Contact Center, Fraud Risk Manager, Head of Compliance
controls.reason: Customer Service is accountable for complaint channels; IT, contact center, social media, and compliance are contributors. Internal Audit verifies via audits of complaint systems.

controls.title: INTERNAL DISPUTE RESOLUTION
controls.control:
- Develop and maintain a formal IDR policy.
- Automate complaint logging and tracking system with timestamped acknowledgment.

controls.additionalControl:

- Incorporate compliance KPIs into staff performance metrics.

controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Chief Compliance Officer (Oversight)- Complaint Resolution Team Lead (Execution)- IT Head (System Support)- Internal Audit (Monitoring & Evaluation)
controls.reason: Compliance is accountable for internal dispute resolution policy; customer experience, operations, and IT are contributors. Internal Audit verifies via regular audits.
