- Use CBN-prescribed beneficial ownership forms
- Cross-check names against sanctions lists and watchlists
- Update beneficial ownership info regularly
- Require organizational charts for complex structures
controls.additionalControl:
- Use digital beneficial ownership registries (e.g., CAC BO portal)
- Implement enhanced due diligence for high-risk entities or jurisdictions
- Require declarations under oath for opaque or layered ownership structures
- Perform media and database checks for red flags in ownership trails
controls.responsibilityText: Relationship Managers, KYC Officers, Compliance Officers, Legal & Corporate Services
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Execution – KYC/Onboarding Team, Relationship OfficersOversight – Compliance Officer, Legal Unit
controls.reason: Verification of beneficial ownership is an AML/CFT compliance control owned by the CCO; KYC/Relationship Officers execute, Legal supports, and Internal Audit verifies.

controls.title: Timing of Verification
controls.control:
- Verify identity documents before or during onboarding wherever possible
- Where post-verification is allowed, ensure 48-hour rule is enforced
- Apply transaction limits and monitoring rules until full verification is done
- Keep logs of exceptions and approvals
- Risk-assess each non-verified onboarding case
controls.additionalControl:
- Automate triggers for blocking accounts if verification exceeds 48 hours
- Escalate unverified accounts to Compliance after 24 hours
- Conduct post-onboarding reviews on all non-face-to-face relationships
- Apply enhanced monitoring on temporary-access accounts
controls.responsibilityText: Account Officers, KYC/Onboarding Team, Compliance Officers
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Execution – Account Opening/KYC TeamsMonitoring – Compliance Officer, Internal Control
controls.reason: Timing of verification is an AML/CFT compliance control owned by the CCO; Account Opening/KYC Teams execute, and Internal Audit monitors.

controls.title: Application of CDD to existing customers
controls.control:
- Use a risk-based schedule to refresh KYC on existing customers
- Monitor account activity to flag changes in operation or large transactions
- Reconfirm customer info when regulatory documentation standards change
- Provide compliance staff access to KYC files and CDD updates
- Maintain audit trail of all KYC updates and decisions
controls.additionalControl:
- Automate reminders for periodic KYC review based on customer risk
- Link transaction monitoring systems to customer profiles to trigger CDD reviews
- Conduct periodic internal audits of CDD compliance for legacy accounts
controls.responsibilityText: Account Officers, Compliance Officer, Relationship Managers, KYC/Operations Unit
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Execution – Account Officers, KYC UnitOversight – Compliance Officer, Internal Audit
controls.reason: Compliance Officer is the most accountable for CDD refresh and KYC oversight; Account Officers, Relationship Managers, and KYC/Operations Unit execute, while Internal Audit provides independent oversight.

controls.title: Failure to Complete CDD
controls.control:
- Transaction screening
- STR procedure and escalation flow
- Staff awareness and training
- Risk-based customer onboarding
controls.additionalControl:
- Enhanced staff training on STR and tipping-off scenarios
- Supervisory approval before continuing risky onboarding
- Internal alert system for flagged relationships
controls.responsibilityText: Compliance Officer, Relationship Officers, AML/CFT Desk
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Execution: Relationship Managers, Operations, and Frontline StaffReporting: Compliance Officer/MLROOversight: Internal Audit and Risk Unit
controls.reason: Compliance Officer/MLRO is accountable for STR procedures and escalation; Relationship Officers, AML/CFT Desk, and frontline staff execute, while Internal Audit and Risk Unit provide oversight.

controls.title: Tiered Know-Your-Customer measures
controls.control:
- Implement tiered KYC levels with specific onboarding rules per CBN’s e-KYC Guidance
- Set daily/monthly transaction limits for each account tier
- Require more detailed documents for accounts with higher usage
- Monitor account activity for deviations from expected behavior
- Use automated flags to escalate suspicious behavior in low-tier accounts
controls.additionalControl:
- Integrate tiered KYC with real-time monitoring tools
- Conduct regular system audits of e-KYC onboarding
- Track account upgrades and revalidate KYC during transitions
- Restrict high-risk transactions (e.g., international wires) on low-tier accounts
controls.responsibilityText: KYC/Onboarding Officers, Compliance Officer, Digital Banking Team, IT/Operations
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Execution – KYC/Digital Onboarding TeamsOversight – Chief Compliance Officer, Internal Control
controls.reason: Chief Compliance Officer has oversight of tiered KYC implementation; KYC/Onboarding Officers and Digital Banking Team execute, with Internal Control and Internal Audit providing oversight.

controls.title: Reliance on intermediaries and third parties on CDD function
controls.control:
- Only rely on third parties that are CBN-compliant and regulated
- Conduct due diligence on third party’s AML/CFT framework
- Sign formal agreements with third parties for CDD obligations
- Require immediate access to all KYC and verification data
- Maintain audit trail of third-party reliance justifications
controls.additionalControl:
- Use a third-party approval register for all CDD dependencies
- Reassess third-party risk annually
- Conduct random spot checks on CDD files from third parties
- Limit reliance to third parties in low-risk jurisdictions or regulated groups
controls.responsibilityText: Relationship Managers, KYC Unit, Compliance Officer, Legal Department
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Execution – KYC Unit, Legal, ComplianceOversight – Chief Compliance Officer, Internal Audit
controls.reason: Chief Compliance Officer oversees third-party CDD reliance; Relationship Managers, KYC Unit, and Legal execute, while Internal Audit provides independent oversight.

controls.title: Application of enhanced due diligence to higher risk customers and activities
controls.control:
- Identify high-risk categories at onboarding using a CBN-aligned risk scoring model
- Collect additional information (e.g., source of funds, wealth, business purpose)
- Get senior management approval before establishing high-risk relationships
- Perform more frequent reviews and transaction monitoring
- Conduct site visits or verify customer declarations independently if necessary
controls.additionalControl:
- Automate flagging of high-risk customers in onboarding platforms
- Integrate PEP screening tools
- Conduct regular training for staff on red flags and EDD procedures
- Maintain an updated internal EDD checklist based on evolving risk categories
controls.responsibilityText: Relationship Managers, KYC Unit, Compliance Officer, Risk Management Department
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Execution – KYC Analysts, Relationship OfficersOversight – Compliance Officer, MLRO (Money Laundering Reporting Officer)
controls.reason: Compliance Officer/MLRO is accountable for EDD application; Relationship Managers, KYC Unit, and Risk Management execute, with Internal Audit providing oversight.

controls.title: Politically Exposed Person (PEP)
controls.control:
- Use PEP screening tools during onboarding and periodic reviews
- Require senior management sign-off before onboarding or continuing PEP relationships
- Obtain verified documents on source of wealth/funds
- Implement automated transaction monitoring for PEP accounts
- Submit monthly PEP returns to CBN/NFIU and report suspicious transactions immediately
controls.additionalControl:
- Conduct periodic independent audits of PEP handling procedures
- Use adverse media checks and international databases to enhance screening
- Review all PEP accounts quarterly, even if no red flags have emerged
- Maintain a separate watchlist for domestic and foreign PEPs
controls.responsibilityText: Relationship Officers, Compliance Officer, KYC Unit, Senior Management
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Execution – KYC Analysts, Relationship ManagersApproval – Senior ManagementOversight – Chief Compliance Officer, MLRO
controls.reason: Chief Compliance Officer/MLRO oversees PEP handling; Relationship Officers, KYC Unit, and Senior Management execute and approve, with Internal Audit providing independent oversight.

controls.title: Cross-border and correspondent banking
controls.control:
- Conduct enhanced CDD on all foreign respondent banks
- Require public and regulatory reputation checks
- Obtain senior management sign-off before onboarding
- Use a correspondent banking questionnaire (e.g. Wolfsberg) to assess AML controls
- Establish documented agreement detailing each party’s AML/CFT responsibilities
controls.additionalControl:
- Conduct annual re-assessments of all correspondent relationships
- Set risk-based limits on transaction volumes or services
- Require periodic attestations from respondent institutions about AML/CFT compliance
- Engage external compliance consultants to validate high-risk correspondent relationships
controls.responsibilityText: Correspondent Banking Desk, Compliance Officer, Risk Management Unit, Senior Management
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Execution – Correspondent Banking/KYC DeskApproval – Senior ManagementOversight – Chief Compliance Officer
controls.reason: Chief Compliance Officer oversees correspondent banking AML/CFT; Correspondent Banking Desk, Compliance Officer, and Risk Management execute, with Internal Audit providing oversight.

controls.title: New technologies and non-face-to-face transactions
controls.control:
- Conduct documented ML/TF risk assessments for all new or modified digital products
- Implement real-time identity verification tools for non-face-to-face onboarding
- Enforce multi-factor authentication and geolocation checks
- Develop procedures specific to virtual banking and remote transactions
- Automate enhanced due diligence (EDD) for remote customer relationships
controls.additionalControl:
- Conduct third-party cybersecurity audits of digital platforms
- Use AI/ML transaction monitoring to detect unusual patterns
- Regularly train staff on emerging risks tied to new tech
- Perform periodic risk re-evaluations post-deployment
controls.responsibilityText: Product Development, IT/Digital Banking, Compliance Officer, Risk Management
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Execution – Product/IT/Digital Teams, Compliance UnitApproval – Chief Compliance Officer, Head of Risk
controls.reason: Chief Compliance Officer and Head of Risk approve new technology risk assessments; Product/IT/Digital Teams and Compliance Unit execute, with Internal Audit providing oversight.

controls.title: Money or Value Transfer (MVT) Services
controls.control:
- Enforce strict licensing of MVTS services through CBN
- Keep and regularly update agent lists, send quarterly returns
- Use AML/CFT due diligence checklists for agents and correspondent partners
- Implement automated monitoring systems for wire transfers
- Validate sender/beneficiary info during onboarding and transaction processing
- Apply screening systems for sanctions lists (UN/CBN/NFIU)
- File STRs when suspicious transactions are flagged across either end of the payment chain
controls.additionalControl:
- Conduct independent audits of MVTS operations semi-annually
- Integrate name screening tools into the wire transfer system
- Train staff on new typologies in value transfer abuse
- Include STR filing timelines in compliance KPIs
controls.responsibilityText: MVTS Compliance Officer, Operations Unit, IT/Transaction Monitoring, Risk & Internal Control, CBN-Licensing Desk
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Execution – MVTS/Remittance Unit, AML DeskOversight – Chief Compliance OfficerApproval – CBN-licensed team & Senior Management
controls.reason: Chief Compliance Officer oversees MVTS AML/CFT; MVTS Compliance Officer, Operations, and IT/Transaction Monitoring execute, with Internal Audit providing independent oversight.

controls.title: Wire Transfers
controls.control:
- Integrate mandatory data fields for wire transfers
- Block submission of wire transfers without required info
- Implement rule-based transaction monitoring
- Maintain automated alerts for incomplete or suspicious wires
- Include screening for terrorist lists (UN/CBN/NFIU)
- Define SOPs for STR filing and rejection of non-compliant transfers
- Maintain 5-year archives of cross-border messages where needed
controls.additionalControl:
- Daily reconciliation of wire transfer records
- Automated alerts for missing originator/beneficiary data
- Quarterly audits of SWIFT and payment messages
- Conduct peer-institution due diligence annually
- Pre-transaction validation checks for high-risk corridors
controls.responsibilityText: Operations, Compliance, Transaction Monitoring, IT, Risk Management
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Execution – Transaction Operations, SWIFT/Payments TeamMonitoring – Compliance Unit, AML DeskOversight – Chief Compliance Officer, Head of Risk
controls.reason: Chief Compliance Officer and Head of Risk oversee wire transfer compliance; Operations, Transaction Monitoring, and IT execute, with Internal Audit providing oversight.

controls.title: Attention to high-risk countries
controls.control:
- Use FATF/CBN lists to flag high-risk countries in the system
- Enforce automated EDD triggers for flagged jurisdictions
- Pre-screen and limit onboarding of clients from these countries
- Block or escalate transactions from flagged regions for review
- Monitor and audit offshore branches in high-risk zones
- Issue internal advisories on specific jurisdictions
controls.additionalControl:
- Subscribe to FATF/CBN watchlist updates
- Establish escalation matrix for high-risk jurisdiction reviews
- Train staff regularly on how to handle clients from high-risk countries
- Restrict third-party reliance in high-risk zones unless cleared by compliance
- Notify CBN proactively on flagged activities involving listed countries
controls.responsibilityText: Compliance Unit, Transaction Monitoring, Legal, International Banking Desk
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Execution – International Banking, EDD Analysts, Compliance OperationsOversight – Chief Compliance Officer, Head of Risk Management
controls.reason: Chief Compliance Officer and Head of Risk Management oversee high-risk country controls; Compliance Unit, Transaction Monitoring, and Legal execute, with Internal Audit providing oversight.

controls.title: Keeping and maintenance of transaction records
controls.control:
- Automate retention of customer and transaction data in central systems
- Implement secure storage and backup protocols (on-prem & cloud)
- Tag and index high-risk or suspicious transactions
- Periodic review of data retention compliance
- Train staff on documentation standards
controls.additionalControl:
- Set up audit trails and change logs for record integrity
- Restrict and monitor access to sensitive records
- Use DLP (Data Loss Prevention) tools
- Include record-keeping review in internal audits
- Maintain offsite or disaster recovery storage
controls.responsibilityText: Compliance Department, IT/Data Management, Records/Archives, Internal Audit
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Execution – IT Data Team, Compliance Operations, Documentation UnitOversight – Chief Compliance Officer (CCO), Head of Risk/Records Management
controls.reason: Chief Compliance Officer oversees record-keeping compliance; IT/Data Management and Records/Archives execute, with Internal Audit providing independent oversight.

controls.title: Recording Identification Evidence
controls.control:
- Automate retention of customer and transaction data in central systems
- Implement secure storage and backup protocols (on-prem & cloud)
- Tag and index high-risk or suspicious transactions
- Periodic review of data retention compliance
- Train staff on documentation standards
controls.additionalControl:
- Set up audit trails and change logs for record integrity
- Restrict and monitor access to sensitive records
- Use DLP (Data Loss Prevention) tools
- Include record-keeping review in internal audits
- Maintain offsite or disaster recovery storage
controls.responsibilityText: Compliance Department, IT/Data Management, Records/Archives, Internal Audit
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Execution – IT Data Team, Compliance Operations, Documentation UnitOversight – Chief Compliance Officer (CCO), Head of Risk/Records Management
controls.reason: Compliance Department is listed first and owns AML/CFT record-keeping; IT, Records, and Internal Audit are contributors. Head of Compliance is the accountable role for AML/CFT compliance oversight.

controls.title: Attention on Complex and Unusual Large Transactions
controls.control:
- Deploy automated transaction monitoring systems with risk flags
- Set account-specific transaction thresholds and alerts
- Conduct manual reviews of flagged transactions
- Maintain a suspicious transaction review log
- Ensure prompt reporting to NFIU
controls.additionalControl:
- Regular staff training on red flags and reporting protocol
- Enhance system learning with new case patterns
- Conduct periodic retrospective reviews of account behavior
- Integrate AI or machine learning for complex transaction pattern recognition
controls.responsibilityText: Transaction Monitoring Unit, Compliance Department, Relationship Managers
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Execution – Transaction Monitoring Unit, Compliance AnalystsOversight – Chief Compliance Officer (CCO), Internal Control/Audit
controls.reason: Transaction monitoring and STR reporting are core AML/CFT compliance functions; Compliance Department is primary. Head of AML/CFT is the accountable role.

controls.title: Evidence of Suspicious Transaction Monitoring
controls.control:
- Automated monitoring system
- Manual alert triggers
- Escalation flow to Compliance
- Immediate STR filing procedures
- Staff whistleblowing protocol
controls.additionalControl:
- Real-time transaction surveillance tools
- Pre-configured terrorist watchlist integration
- Periodic drills/simulations of response timeline
controls.responsibilityText: AML/CFT Compliance Officer, Transaction Monitoring Unit, IT Surveillance Team
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Detection & Escalation: Operations & Frontline StaffDocumentation & Reporting: AML/CFT Compliance UnitOversight: Internal Control & Risk Department
controls.reason: AML/CFT Compliance Officer and Transaction Monitoring Unit are within Compliance; IT Surveillance is a contributor. Head of AML/CFT is accountable.

controls.title: Procedure for the Monitoring and Reporting of Suspicious Transactions
controls.control:
- Written suspicious transaction monitoring and reporting policy
- Automated transaction monitoring tools
- Checklist of known red flags and typologies
- Prompt review and escalation by Compliance Officer
- STR reporting workflow integrated into core systems
- Staff confidentiality agreement and awareness
controls.additionalControl:
- Periodic refresher training on suspicious activity detection
- Internal STR quality reviews
- Surprise audits on high-risk units
- Scenario-based simulations and drills
controls.responsibilityText: Compliance Department, Operations Team, Frontline Staff, Chief Compliance Officer
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Execution – Compliance Officer, AML Analysts, Business Unit StaffOversight – Chief Compliance Officer, Internal Audit
controls.reason: Compliance Department owns the suspicious transaction monitoring and reporting policy; Operations and Frontline are execution contributors. Head of Compliance is accountable.

controls.title: Other Forms of Reporting
controls.control:
- Threshold-based transaction monitoring tools
- Automated alerts and reporting templates
- Escalation protocol to Compliance for vetting and filing
- Staff awareness of secrecy/confidentiality rule
controls.additionalControl:
- Daily reconciliation reports flagged for high-value/foreign transfers
- System controls for mandatory flagging
- Internal audit spot checks
- Legal advisory on nondisclosure obligations
controls.responsibilityText: AML/CFT Compliance Officer, Transaction Monitoring Unit, Operations/Remittance Team
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Triggering & Initial Review: Front Office, Operations TeamFinal Filing & Reporting: AML/CFT Compliance OfficerOversight: Head of Compliance / Internal Control
controls.reason: Final filing and reporting is by AML/CFT Compliance Officer under Head of Compliance; Operations and Front Office trigger and review. Compliance is accountable.

controls.title: AML, CFT and CPF Employee Awareness and Training Programme
controls.control:
- Documented AML/CFT/CPF training policy
- Scheduled onboarding and refresher trainings
- Training attendance records
- Role-specific training modules
- Quarterly compliance reporting to CBN
- Management review of training effectiveness
controls.additionalControl:
- Use of computer-based training platforms
- Training assessment quizzes or exams
- Scenario-based simulations and case studies
- Annual board-level AML/CFT/CPF training reviews
controls.responsibilityText: Compliance Officer, Human Resources (HR), Training Department, Departmental Heads
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Execution – Compliance Officer, Training Team, HROversight – Chief Compliance Officer, Executive Management
controls.reason: Compliance Officer owns AML/CFT training policy and reporting; HR and Training deliver. Head of Compliance is accountable for the programme.

controls.title: Monitoring of Employee Conduct
controls.control:
- Whistleblowing policy and reporting channels
- Internal control mechanisms
- Surveillance systems/log review
- Disciplinary procedures
- Regular staff conduct reviews
- Monitoring logs
controls.additionalControl:
- Surprise audits
- Conflict-of-interest declarations
- Ethics and conduct training
- Anonymous employee behavior hotlines
- Background checks for high-risk roles
controls.responsibilityText: Compliance Department, Internal Control/Audit, HR, Line Managers
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Monitoring & Detection – Compliance Officer, Internal Audit, Line ManagersDisciplinary Oversight – HR, Executive Management
controls.reason: Employee conduct monitoring is a Compliance/Conduct & Ethics function; HR handles disciplinary oversight. Head of Compliance is accountable.

controls.title: Protection of Staff Who Report Violation
controls.control:
- Whistleblower protection policy
- Anonymous reporting channels
- Legal assurance of protection from liability
- Staff training on whistleblower rights
controls.additionalControl:
- Third-party-operated whistleblower hotline
- Periodic assurance notices to staff
- Whistleblower policy awareness campaigns
controls.responsibilityText: Compliance Unit, HR Department, Legal Department
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Policy Oversight – Legal/ComplianceEnforcement & HR protection – Human ResourcesAwareness/Training – Compliance Unit
controls.reason: Whistleblower protection policy is owned by Compliance/Legal; HR enforces protection. Compliance is primary accountable, but Legal and HR compete, lowering confidence.

controls.title: Client Accounts Opened by Professional Intermediaries
controls.control:
- Pre-qualification of intermediaries (regulatory status and AML controls)
- CDD documentation request logs
- Independent review of intermediary’s AML/CFT systems
controls.additionalControl:
- Annual review and audit of intermediary CDD practices
- legal agreement outlining intermediary’s CDD responsibilities
- immediate fallback protocol if doubts arise about CDD quality
controls.responsibilityText: Compliance Officer, Customer Onboarding Team, Relationship Managers
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Control/Review – Compliance UnitExecution – Account Opening TeamMonitoring – Internal Audit/Legal
controls.reason: Compliance Officer controls intermediary CDD and AML review; Onboarding and Relationship Managers execute. Head of Compliance is accountable.

controls.title: Unincorporated Business or Partnership
controls.control:
- Mandatory KYC forms for each partner
- Verification of business location
- Review of audited accounts
- Mandate authorization for partnership accounts
controls.additionalControl:
- Require tax identification or registration with CAC
- Periodic account activity monitoring
- Cross-verification with regulatory or licensing bodies
controls.responsibilityText: Account Opening Team, Compliance Officer, Relationship Managers
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Execution – Account OfficersVerification – Compliance TeamMonitoring – Internal Audit/Branch Ops
controls.reason: Compliance Officer verifies KYC for partnerships; Account Opening executes. Head of Compliance is accountable for AML/CFT CDD.

controls.title: Limited Liability Partnership
controls.control: Current CDD/KYC procedures for corporate accounts; customer classification checklists
controls.additionalControl: Periodic account classification reviews, staff training on identifying LLPs during onboarding
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Head of Compliance, Head of Operations
controls.reason: Compliance owns CDD/KYC procedures for LLP accounts; Account Opening and Legal contribute. Head of Compliance is accountable.

controls.title: Pure Corporate Customers
controls.control: Current corporate account onboarding checklist; CAC search; beneficial ownership registry checks
controls.additionalControl: Enhanced due diligence (EDD) triggers for unclear ownership; cross-checking with tax records and business activity verification
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Head of Compliance, Head of Legal, Head of Operations
controls.reason: Compliance owns corporate onboarding CDD and beneficial ownership checks; Legal and Operations contribute. Head of Compliance is accountable.

controls.title: The Identity of  corporate company
controls.control: Corporate account KYC checklist; CAC search process; beneficial ownership verification; SCUML validation
controls.additionalControl: Automated corporate verification tools; periodic re-verification; cross-check with FIRS tax database
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Head of Compliance, Head of Operations, Head of Legal
controls.reason: Compliance leads corporate KYC and beneficial ownership verification; Account Opening Unit and Legal are contributors. Head of Compliance is accountable.

controls.title: Non Face -to Face  Business
controls.control: Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) policy; remote verification procedures; customer onboarding checklist
controls.additionalControl: Implement video KYC tools; cross-check addresses with utility bills and third-party verification databases; mandatory escalation for high-risk cases
controls.responsibilityText: Compliance, Account Opening Unit, E-Business Operations, Legal
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Head of Compliance, Head of Operations, Head of E-Business
controls.reason: Compliance owns EDD policy for non-face-to-face business; other units contribute. Head of Compliance is accountable.

controls.title: Public Registered Companies
controls.control:
- board resolution/authorization for representatives
- confirmation call to CEO (where applicable)
- risk-based due diligence on services requested
- screening of company and directors against watchlists
controls.additionalControl:
- Periodic re-validation of authorized signatories
- Monitoring of high-risk transactions
- Internal whistleblowing channels for misuse of company names
controls.responsibilityText: Corporate Banking Team, Compliance Officer, KYC/Onboarding Unit
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Execution – Corporate Account OfficerVerification – Compliance TeamMonitoring – Internal Audit/Transaction Monitoring Unit
controls.reason: Compliance Officer is explicitly responsible for verification; Corporate Banking and KYC/Onboarding execute. Internal Audit monitors.

controls.title: Higher Risk Business Applicant
controls.control:
- Mandatory CAC search or third-party legal verification
- Collection of Board resolution and incorporation documents
- Review of audited accounts for legitimacy
- KYC/EDD screening based on risk
controls.additionalControl:
- Independent background checks via external risk intelligence platforms
- Internal risk rating score for account approval
- Senior Management review before account activation
controls.responsibilityText: Account Opening/Onboarding Unit, Corporate Banking Team, Compliance Officer
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Execution – Corporate Banking/Relationship ManagerVerification – Compliance & Legal UnitMonitoring – Internal Audit/EDD Monitoring Team
controls.reason: Compliance Officer verifies higher-risk applicants; onboarding and corporate banking execute. Internal Audit monitors.

controls.title: Higher Risk Business Relating to Private Companies
controls.control:
- Mandatory identification of 5%+ shareholders and beneficial owners
- Corporate structure and trust transparency checks
- Periodic updates and site verification
- Risk-based screening of directors and signatories
- Enhanced monitoring of account activity and changes
controls.additionalControl:
- Offshore entity vetting using international databases
- Senior Management sign-off for onboarding IBCs or high-risk clients
- Legal opinion on trust or layered ownership structures
- Trigger-based review mechanism for changes in shareholding or activity
controls.responsibilityText: Corporate Banking Team, Relationship Managers, Compliance Unit, KYC Officers
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Execution – Account Officer/Corporate RMVerification – Compliance/KYC TeamMonitoring – Internal Audit/Risk Control Function
controls.reason: Compliance Unit verifies beneficial ownership and risk screening; corporate banking and RMs execute. Internal Audit monitors.

controls.title: Foreign Financial Institutions
controls.control: Foreign Correspondent Bank KYC policy; SWIFT KYC checks
controls.additionalControl: Automate regulator-lookup process; maintain database of vetted foreign banks
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Head of Compliance, Intl. Banking Head
controls.reason: Compliance owns foreign correspondent bank KYC; International Banking contributes. Head of Compliance accountable.

controls.title: Bureau De Change
controls.control: EDD policy for high-risk customers
controls.additionalControl: Annual BDC license re-verification with CBN
controls.reason: Compliance owns EDD for bureau de change; Treasury Ops contributes. Head of Compliance accountable.

controls.title: Designated Non-financial Businesses and Professions(DNFBs)
controls.control: SCUML verification checklist
controls.additionalControl: Add SCUML expiry-date tracking; trigger re-verification
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Head of Compliance, Branch Ops Manager
controls.reason: Compliance owns SCUML verification for DNFBPs; Retail Banking contributes. Head of Compliance accountable.

controls.title: Occupational Pension Schemes
controls.control: Corporate customer KYC procedures
controls.additionalControl: Add trustee verification template; periodic source-of-funds check
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Head of Compliance, Institutional Banking Head
controls.reason: Compliance owns KYC for pension schemes; Institutional Banking contributes. Head of Compliance accountable.

controls.title: Registered Charity Organizations
controls.control:
- Mandatory verification of registration and address of the charity
- Minimum of two signatories required and verified
- Notification to and confirmation from official correspondent when necessary
- Use of club/society procedures for unregistered organizations
- KYC review upon any change in signatory
controls.additionalControl:
- Periodic review of charity accounts and beneficiaries
- Real-time monitoring for high-risk donations or foreign inflows
- Screening of signatories and the organization against watchlists
controls.responsibilityText: Account Opening Officers, Relationship Managers, Compliance Officers
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Execution: Relationship Manager / Account OfficerVerification: Compliance / KYC UnitMonitoring: Internal Audit / Internal Control
controls.reason: Compliance Officers verify charity registration and signatories; account opening and RMs execute. Internal Audit monitors.

controls.title: Religious Organizations
controls.control: Customer onboarding checklist for NPOs
controls.additionalControl: Add annual re-verification of CAC & SCUML status; maintain denominational verification contacts
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Head of Compliance, Branch Ops Manager
controls.reason: Compliance owns onboarding checklist for religious organizations; Retail Banking contributes. Head of Compliance accountable.

controls.title: Three-Tiers of Government and Parastatals
controls.control:
- Verify legal identity and address
- Obtain valid authorizations and resolutions
- Conduct telephone confirmation with CEO
- Require Accountant-General’s authorization prior to account opening
controls.additionalControl:
- Use government KYC checklist
- Monitor inflows and usage of public funds
- Regular review and revalidation of signatory and authorization documents
controls.responsibilityText: Relationship Manager, Public Sector Banking Unit, Compliance Officer
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Execution: Public Sector Desk / Relationship OfficerVerification: Compliance / Legal UnitMonitoring: Internal Control / Audit
controls.reason: Compliance Officer verifies government accounts; Public Sector Desk and RM execute. Internal Audit monitors.

controls.title: Foreign  Consulates
controls.control: Contact protocol with MFA and diplomatic channels
controls.additionalControl: Maintain updated MFA liaison list; periodic training on diplomatic account handling
controls.reason: Primary responsibility text lists Compliance and Corporate Banking; Compliance is the accountable function for AML/CFT contact protocols with MFA, and Head of Compliance is named in additional responsibility.

controls.title: Intermediaries or other third parties to verify identity or to introduce business
controls.control: Interbank KYC reliance agreements; AML/CFT policy
controls.additionalControl: Require periodic due diligence reviews on relied-upon FIs; document evidence of reliance
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Head of Compliance, Branch Ops Manager
controls.reason: Compliance is listed first and Head of Compliance is named in additional responsibility; Branch Ops is a contributor for execution.

controls.act: Money Laundering (Prevention and Prohibition) Act, 2022
controls.title: Duty to report international transfer or transportation of funds, securities and cash
controls.control:
- Threshold-based automated alerts for US$10,000+ transfers
- Mandatory review by Compliance before processing international transactions
- Record-keeping of reports sent to regulators
- Standard operating procedures (SOPs) for reporting timelines
controls.additionalControl:
- Daily transaction exception reports reviewed by Compliance
- Training staff on identifying and processing high-value international transfers
- Periodic internal audit reviews of all such transfers and declarations
- Client education materials at teller points and on digital platforms
controls.responsibilityText: Compliance Department, International Remittance/Trade Unit, Customer Service, Risk Management
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: Compliance Officer (report filing), Head of Operations (oversight), IT Team (automation), Audit Committee (independent review)
controls.reason: Compliance Department is listed first and Compliance Officer is named for report filing; other units are contributors. Internal Audit is named for independent review.

controls.title: Identification of customers
controls.control:
- Standard KYC procedures and onboarding checklist
- Use of centralized verification systems (e.g., NIN, BVN, CAC, passports)

controls.control:

- Require written NSC approval before executing any debit or release.

- Conduct periodic compliance audits of all frozen fund approvals.
- Maintain a secure archive of all NSC approvals and reports sent.

controls.reason: Head of Compliance oversees frozen fund release approvals; Operations executes and Legal validates NSC directives.

controls.title: Reporting Requirements
controls.control:
- Implement automated systems to detect and flag blocked, rejected, or failed transactions involving designated names.
- Maintain a log of attempted transactions tied to CDD failures or sanctions list matches.
- Escalate all flagged incidents to Compliance for review and STR filing.

controls.control:

controls.title: System Integration & Scalability
controls.control:

- Ensure AML system includes secure APIs or data ports for other system connections.
- Conduct integration testing with all target systems (e.g., core banking, KYC, STR reporting).
- Build data import/export utilities for non-integrated systems.
- Use encryption protocols for secure data transmission.

- Maintain documentation and logs for data transfers and system linkages.
- Assign dedicated IT compliance liaisons to ensure smooth integration with future platforms.

controls.control:

- Implement AI-fuzzy matching engines for effective name-matching.
- Set up automated pipelines to ensure real-time sanctions list updates.
- Maintain and regularly update internal watchlists.
- Integrate and periodically update PEP databases from credible global sources.
- Activate adverse media scanning tools and link to internal case management systems.
controls.additionalControl:
- Conduct regular tuning and validation of fuzzy match algorithms to minimize false positives/negatives.
- Carry out internal audits of sanction list updates and screening processes.
- Train staff on interpreting AI-flagged results and adverse media alerts.
- Monitor vendor reliability for sanctions list feed and data quality.

controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Compliance Technology Team - AML Screening Team - Internal Audit (for independent review)

controls.title: Transaction Monitoring & Risk-Based Analysis
controls.control:
- Conduct regular stress testing and scenario analysis on AML transaction monitoring systems.
- Define a measurable benchmark (e.g., ≤10% false positives) as a threshold for system performance.
- Implement system tuning protocols to optimize detection rules and minimize false positives.
- Use AI/ML analytics to improve risk detection precision.
controls.additionalControl:
- Maintain a dashboard to track false positive metrics and performance trends.
- Engage external validators or third-party auditors for independent performance testing.
- Conduct root cause analysis on spikes in false positives and retrain detection models.

controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Compliance Risk Team - AML Monitoring Unit - Data Science/Analytics Team - External System Validator (where used)

The raw text lists Head of Compliance, AML Systems Analyst, Internal Audit, and Head of IT Risk Management, but the most accountable is Compliance.

- Periodic penetration testing and system audit to verify integrity of integrations.

- Include machine conformity checks as part of internal and external audits.

controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Head of Procurement & Equipment - Head of Operations - Chief Compliance Officer - CBN Monitoring Desk Liaison
controls.reason: Currency processing machine inventory and calibration is operational. Head of Operations named. IT, Procurement, Compliance contribute. Internal Audit verifies.

controls.title: Automated Teller Machines (ATMs)
controls.control:
- Ensure ATMs are loaded only with authenticated and fitness-checked notes.
- Conduct routine testing and servicing of ATM sensors for counterfeit detection.
- Use certified sorting machines before ATM loading.
- Maintain an audit trail of cash loading and source of notes.
controls.additionalControl:
- Integrate real-time ATM monitoring for note rejection or customer complaints.
- Periodically retrain ATM custodians and cash handlers.
- Introduce mystery shopping exercises to detect breaches.
- Include ATM note quality check in internal audit scope.
controls.responsibilityText: - Head of ATM Operations - Cash Management/Branch Operations Team - IT Infrastructure Unit - Compliance Unit
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - ATM Service Manager - Operations Risk Officer - Internal Audit Team - Compliance/CBN Liaison Desk
controls.reason: ATM cash loading and fitness checks are cash operations. Head of ATM Operations and Cash Management team named. IT, Compliance, Internal Audit contribute. Internal Audit verifies.

controls.title: Counterfeit Notes Discovered
controls.control:
- Train staff on currency authentication techniques.
- Use CBN-approved currency processing machines with counterfeit detection features.
- Establish a standard operating procedure (SOP) for handling and forwarding counterfeit notes.
- Log and maintain records of all counterfeit incidents.
controls.additionalControl:
- Conduct random reviews of branch-level currency transactions.
- Establish a central counterfeit reporting log across branches.
- Ensure counterfeit notes are tagged with relevant incident reports and forwarded to CBN within stipulated time.
- Include counterfeit incident reporting in audit reviews.
controls.responsibilityText: - Branch Operations Manager - Cash & Treasury Management Team - Internal Control Officer - Compliance Department
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Cash Officers - Operations Risk Manager - Internal Audit Team - CBN Compliance Liaison
controls.reason: Counterfeit notes handling is cash operations. Branch Operations Manager and Cash & Treasury Management Team named. Compliance, Internal Audit contribute. Internal Audit verifies.

controls.title: Mutilated Banknotes Management
controls.control:
- Train branch staff on CBN-approved mutilated note handling procedures.
- Maintain a copy of the CBN Operational Manual at all cash-handling branches.
- Use special handling forms and reporting templates for all such transactions.
- Keep proper documentation and audit trail for every mutilated note received or replaced.
controls.additionalControl:
- Schedule periodic refresher training on handling of mutilated notes.
- Perform surprise audits on branches' mutilated notes management processes.
- Integrate mutilated note processing into internal audit scope.
controls.responsibilityText: - Branch Operations Manager - Cash Officers / Tellers - Treasury Department - Compliance Unit
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Head of Operations - Cash Management Unit - Audit & Internal Control
controls.reason: Primary responsibility lists Branch Operations Manager and Cash Officers/Tellers under Branch Operations; Head of Operations is accountable for branch cash handling. Treasury and Compliance are contributors. Internal Audit verifies via surprise audits and audit scope integration.

controls.title: Publicity Campaign
controls.control:
- Integrate CBN sensitization themes in internal campaigns and customer touchpoints.
- Train frontline staff on clean note policy and security features of genuine notes.
- Monitor and prevent issuance of unfit or dirty notes from ATMs and counters.
- Display anti-naira abuse messages in banking halls and on digital platforms.
controls.additionalControl:
- Partner with CBN in joint customer engagement activities.
- Publish quarterly updates on clean note initiatives and performance.
- Use educational infographics in branches and ATMs.
controls.responsibilityText: - Corporate Communications Unit - Operations Department - Branch Operations Managers - Compliance Department
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Head of Corporate Affairs/Communication - Customer Service Management Team - Cash Management Unit
controls.reason: Publicity campaign spans Operations and Compliance; frontline training and ATM monitoring fall under Operations. Corporate Communications is not in org structure, so best fit is Operations/Customer Service. Compliance verifies adherence to CBN sensitization themes.

controls.act: Penalty for Payment of Counterfeit Banknotes from ATMs/Teller Points
controls.title: COD/DIR/GEN/CMF/18/095
controls.control:
- Use CBN-approved cash processing machines that verify authenticity.
- Implement regular fitness sorting and counterfeit detection protocols.
- Conduct routine spot testing of ATM dispensed notes.
- Train staff and custodians on CBN's Clean Note Policy.
controls.additionalControl:
- Conduct internal ATM inspections weekly.
- Introduce mystery shopper checks for teller cash quality.
- Keep a log of ATM/teller cash sorting dates and quality certifications.
controls.responsibilityText: - Cash Management Department - ATM Custodians/Operations Teams - Branch Managers - Internal Audit & Compliance Departments
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Head of Operations & Technology - Head of Cash & Treasury - Compliance & Risk Units
controls.reason: Cash Management Department is primary for ATM/teller counterfeit detection and sorting. Head of Cash Operations is accountable. Internal Audit and Compliance are listed as contributors but Internal Audit is the independent verifier for ATM inspections and logs.

controls.act: Updated Penalty on Inappropriate Cash Disbursement Practices by Deposit Money Banks (DMBs)
controls.title: COD/DIR/INT/CIR/001/025
controls.control:
- Implement dual authorization for all disbursements of mint notes.
- Maintain detailed logs of mint note inflows and disbursement.
- Conduct internal surveillance of teller and vault operations.
- Limit mint notes to customer-requested withdrawals only.
controls.additionalControl:
- Deploy CCTV and biometric access controls at cash centres.
- Carry out mystery shopper testing internally to assess adherence.
- Train staff on legal implications and ethics around mint note handling.
controls.responsibilityText: - Head of Cash Management - Branch Managers - Teller Supervisors - Internal Control & Audit Units
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - COO/Head of Operations - Cash Management Department - Internal Audit/Compliance Units
controls.reason: Head of Cash Management is primary for mint note disbursement controls. Branch Managers and Teller Supervisors contribute. Internal Audit/Compliance Units verify; Internal Audit is the independent verifier for surveillance and mystery shopper testing.

controls.act: Treatment of Composed Banknotes
controls.title: COD/DIR/INT/CIR/001/006
controls.control:
- Use CBN-approved cash sorting machines with image sensors to detect composed notes.
- Ensure manual verification by trained staff for doubtful notes.
- Maintain segregated logs for suspected mutilated or composed notes.
controls.additionalControl:
- Conduct training for cash handlers on identifying composed notes.
- Sample-check deposits before dispatch to CBN.
- Implement pre-deposit audit checks for all boxes of notes.
controls.responsibilityText: - Head of Cash Operations - Vault/Treasury Officers - Cash Sorting Units - Branch Managers
controls.additionalResponsibilityText: - Cash Processing Officers - Head of Operations - Compliance & Internal Control Unit
controls.reason: Head of Cash Operations is accountable for composed banknote detection and sorting. Vault/Treasury Officers and Cash Sorting Units contribute. Compliance & Internal Control Unit listed, but Internal Audit is the independent verifier for pre-deposit audit checks.
